title: Workshop on titled “Genome editing technology and its application in farm animals” : (3/22/2021)
body: Division of Innovation and Entrepreneurship is organizing a 3-day online workshop on titled “Genome editing technology and its application in farm animals”. The workshop will enable the students to aware about the recently developed technique of genome editing, which has the potential to revolutionize the biotechnological research in many aspects. The technique can be used in dairy animals with a goal to enhance milk yield and make the cows and buffaloes resistant to many diseases. This technique has also applicability in goat, pig and poultry farming to enhance the meat and egg production. title: Believe in yourself and boost your confidence Shared by psychologists from Counseling & happiness cell . (Ref. No. LPU/DSR/IC/210319/002) : (3/19/2021)
body: Dear Students, Believing in yourself in the secret to success. The ability to believe in yourself can change your life. “Believe in yourself. You are braver than you think, more talented than you know, and capable of more than you imagine.” “Low self-esteem is like driving through life with your hand brake on.” -- Maxwell Maltz Nobody is born with limitless self-confidence. If someone seems to have incredible self-confidence, it’s because he or she has worked on building it for years. Self-confidence is something that you learn to build up due to the life challenges, and can deflate it. Your thoughts become words and your words become your actions. If you continue to tell yourself that you believe in yourself, eventually you really will believe in yourself. By believing in yourself, you will find the courage to take immediate action on your goals. And this, as you may know, is the key to success! Psychologists from counseling & happiness cell - share tips to help students build self-confidence. We care about your emotional and psychological well-being. Please email us – counseling.happiness@lpu.co.in PFA – Believe in yourself

body: There are many potential causes of academic stress, including: Achievement Anxiety • Achievement anxiety refers to a fear of failure in an academic setting. • It sometimes occurs if a student fails to meet academic expectations set by parents, peers, teachers, or even the students themselves. If you are feeling academic stress and want to learn strategies to cope with academic pressure, then this webinar is for you. title: LPU Global: Opportunity to spend a semester abroad at 100% tuition fee scholarship : (3/15/2021)
body: Division of International Affairs brings great opportunity for LPU students of various program in the attached list to attend a fully tuition fee waived semester at partner foreign University i.e. students have to pay only tuition fees applicable at LPU and they get opportunity to study for one semester at partner University in Canada, France, Sweden, Lithuania etc. without paying tuition fees of partner university. All formalities and fees relating to VISA, travel, accommodation, food and any other fees of the partner foreign University has to be borne by the student. Details of available institutions are attached. Eligibility: · Minimum CGPA 6.5 with no backlogs and reappearances · Regular Attendance · Active Participant in extracurricular activities · Excellent communication skills · Capacity to Sustain himself/herself overseas while studying (Estimated budget 2 Lakh to 4 Lakh depending on country and university of choice · A valid Passport Interested students must fill the form before: 20th March 2021 https://forms.gle/xgyNcGR1kTwUwgoc9 Please Note: · Selection would be based on multi-level interviews · Student can apply only to one university at a time for second university please fill the form again · Seats would be filled on first in-first out basis and are fully at the discretion of selection committee at LPU & partner University There can be possibility of online, offline or hybrid classes by the partner university. For further information please contact Division of International Affairs at studyabroad@lpu.co.in

title: Regarding preference polling of Engineering Minors for Autumn Term 2021-22 (Ref. No. LPU/DOE/IC/210308/001) : (3/8/2021)
body: Dear Students, It is mandatory for all the students of all engineering programs currently in their fourth term to select an Engineering Minor of their choice. Note that under each engineering minor, a group of 4 courses is offered which the student shall be studying from their 5th term onwards. The selection of an engineering minor area shall automatically lead to selection of these 4 corresponding courses in that area. In order to facilitate the students to make the choice when the polling for engineering minors starts, School wise folder of list of engineering minors to be offered to you is available at the link: Important Links---->Examination Instructions and Guidelines---->Engineering Minor Folder Students can also view the recorded Engineering Minor Session held for you on Myclass platform. Details of the session held is mentioned on the first page of the interface. With regard to the same, all the students are compulsorily required to participate in the polling process for Engineering Minor. The link to participate in preference polling is given below- UMS Home:- UMS Navigation--->Learning Management System--->Engineering Minor Area Preference. UMS Dashboard:- Academics--->Learning Management System--->Engineering Minor Area Preference. Or through LPU TOUCH app at the link “EM Area Preference” The polling schedule, EM allocation criteria and User Manual for using polling interface are attached below. Kindly check the excel sheet Polling Schedule School wise for the start and end date of polling. For any query, please contact your school Academic Operations Coordinator (AOC) on the email ID as per list attached below. title: Mind-2-Market-a virtual ideathon competition : (3/8/2021)
body: Division of Innovation and Entrepreneurship comes up with an exciting event “Mind-2-Market”. Mind-2-Market is a virtual ideathon competition with a vision of converting ideas from Mind –to-Market. So, if you have a brilliant idea for a solution to any societal problem or a new product. You feel energized, inspired, and ready to forge ahead. Then your first challenge is to ‘pitch your idea’. The goal of the event is to home the innovative ideas and turn those ideas into reality. The participants are expected to come up with their best ideas and pitch them in front of the experts. The selected best teams are expected to create a road map of their business, navigating through the opportunities present in the market and by presenting and overcoming the inevitable obstacles an entrepreneur might face, besides developing strategies to avoid problems before they arise. Registration Fee: Rs 200/- per team. Get registered at:: http://tiny.cc/mind2market Last Date of Registration 23rd March.2021 Submit your idea to - anita.23401@lpu.co.in Last date of abstract submission 25th March,2021 Eligibility: All who have brilliant ideas General Rules ? Participants can register as a team of 2-4. ? Only 1 Team will be allowed to participate per college. ? Judges’ decision will be considered final and binding. ? Filling of Online Registration Form: All the students having R grade in the list of courses attached are required to apply online for the registration in R grade and pay the R grade registration fee online via visiting following UMS Link: UMS Navigation----> Examination System------> Exam Registration------> R grade courses Registration The Last date for R grade registration and fee payment is 11th March (without any late fee) and 18th March 2021 (with late fee of Rs.2000/-). title: Registration for Ph.D. End Term Presentation (ETP) (Ref. No. LPU/DOE/IC/210304/003) : (3/4/2021)
body: This is in reference to the Ph.D. End Term Presentation (ETP) evaluation which shall be tentatively scheduled from April 2021 onwards (exact dates will be shared in due course of time). All the research scholars who have registered for their respective Ph.D. programs after July 2016 and have successfully completed their State of the Art Seminar (SAS) evaluation are required to appear for End Term Presentation (ETP) after each 6 months from the date of successful completion of SAS. The main aim of the End Term Presentation is as follows: a. To present the action taken against the recommendations given by the Research Advisory Committee (RAC) in the last evaluation. b. Justification in case a particular suggestion is not incorporated c. To present amount of work done or progress made since last evaluation The research scholars are required to follow the following two steps for appearing in ETP: Step-1. Registration and uploading of ETP reports All eligible research scholars as per the attached list (List of research scholars eligible for ETP) are required to register for ETP evaluation and upload their files through following UMS link: UMS Navigation -->Research & Development --> Ph.D. Scholar Activity Details --> Upcoming Activity The last date for registration and uploading of report is 27th March 2021. Step-2. Recommendation of ETP Report by the respective Supervisor/Co-supervisor/ Administrative supervisor: Once the research scholar have registered for the ETP and uploaded their ETP report for the evaluation, the same must be recommended by their respective Supervisor/Co-supervisor/Administrative supervisor by visiting the following the link: UMS navigation --> Division of Examination --> Ph.D. Evaluation Cell --> PhD Seminar File Verification --> ETP The last date for verification of the report is 31st March 2021. Evaluation of the End Term Presentation (ETP) via online platform It is for the information of the all concerned that due to the prevailing situation, the End Term Presentation (ETP) evaluation shall be planned via online platform google meet. Important Note: For Registration and Uploading of ETP report: 1. As per current guidelines, the research scholars who are either absent or are not recommended in any Ph.D. evaluation 2 times in a row or 3 times overall, the Ph.D. admission may be deemed cancelled. Therefore, all such research scholars who have either missed or have been awarded “Not Recommended” in one or two Ph.D. evaluations are strongly advised to register for the ETP evaluation. 2. The research scholars must upload single PDF file for end term report strictly as per the attached guidelines (Guidelines for ETP) to complete the registration process or else their registration may be cancelled. 3. In case the research scholars are unable to get a signed copy of the synopsis from their respective supervisor due to prevailing situation, they can upload the soft copy of the synopsis without supervisor signature. But it is required that the synopsis uploaded by them must be strictly as per the guidelines and it must be verified by their supervisor through UMS interface as per prescribed timelines. 4. Research scholars are also required to submit 2 hard copies of the reports duly verified and signed by the respective supervisor/ co-supervisor/ administrative supervisor (wherever applicable) in Research Degree and Evaluation Cell (RDEC) (Block-30; Room Number- 302B) for which the separate communication shall be made in due course of time. 5. File containing PDF of snapshots of pages is strictly prohibited and shall not be considered for evaluation. 6. No extension shall be given for registration for ETP beyond the last date. 7. Research scholars should go through the attachment (Snapshots for using ETP registration interface) before registering and uploading the ETP reports at the interface. For Recommendation of the ETP Report: 1. The research scholar must upload the ETP report well in advance so that it can be recommended by the respective Supervisor/Co-supervisor/Administrative supervisor within the stipulated timelines. For online evaluation of the End Term Presentation (ETP) a) The research scholar must have laptop/ desktop or any other suitable mean with proper audio/ video facility. b) The research scholar must have high speed internet facility to appear for the online ETP evaluation. In case, the research scholar has registered for the ETP evaluation but could not appear for the same due to any issue, he/she shall be marked absent for the evaluation. Result of all such research scholars for ETP evaluation shall stand as “Not Recommended” and the will be required to re-register for the next scheduled ETP evaluation with subject to meeting all other eligibility criteria. c) The research scholar must be well versed with the online google meet platform. It is strongly advised that the research scholar must present his/ her presentation to the respective supervisor prior to appearing in actual ETP evaluation so that there is no confusion on the day of evaluation. In case, any of the eligible research scholars has query, write us at rdc.etrs@lpu.co.in

title: Equality Hackathon : (3/4/2021)
body: For more than a century, people around the world have celebrated International Women’s Day on March 8th. It’s a day to focus on the achievements of women, and continue the fight for global equality. Student Research and Project Cell under the aegis of Division of Student Welfare is upcoming with an event titled “Equality Hackathon” to celebrate the Women’s Day. This event will provide opportunity to students to pitch their innovative solutions for some real life issues facing by the women of our country.The best ideas will incubated by SRPC and also rewarded with some exciting prizes. There are Four Tracks: Health: Hack a solution that will help women access health and hygiene resources Physical Safety: Hack a solution that advances women’s physical safety Psychological Safety: Hack a solution that advances women's psychological safety Financial Safety: Hack a solution that will empower women financially. Note: The solution could be a product, a service, or a business idea. Each team needs to identify only “one” track. Round 1: Prelims - Online Solution Submission 1) Submission of Idea via mail @mandeep.16853@lpu.co.in. 2) The team will need to mention the track that they wish to apply to in the document. Round 2: Idea Presentation 1) The teams will have to give a maximum 10 min presentation which includes team member details, possible solution, implementation plan, and the cost. 2) The presentation will be followed by Q&A session. Last Date of Submission of Idea :8th March 2021 Event Day: 9th Mar,2021, 5:30 pm -7:30 pm Registration Link: http://tiny.cc/equalityhack Note: The idea should be submitted in PDF format and the document must comprise of name and registration number. title: LPU Global: Opportunity to spend a semester abroad at 100% tuition fee scholarship : (3/3/2021)
body: Division of International Affairs brings great opportunity for LPU students of various program in the attached list to attend a fully tuition fee waived semester at partner foreign University i.e. students have to pay only tuition fees applicable at LPU and they get opportunity to study for one semester at partner University in Canada, France, Sweden, Lithuania etc. without paying tuition fees of partner university. All formalities and fees relating to VISA, travel, accommodation, food and any other fees of the partner foreign University has to be borne by the student. Details of available institutions are attached. Eligibility: · Minimum CGPA 6.5 with no backlogs and reappearances · Regular Attendance · Active Participant in extracurricular activities · Excellent communication skills · Capacity to Sustain himself/herself overseas while studying (Estimated budget 2 Lakh to 3.5 Lakh depending on country and university of choice) · A valid Passport Interested students must fill the form before 15th March 2021 https://forms.gle/xgyNcGR1kTwUwgoc9 Please Note: · Selection would be based on multi-level interviews · Student can apply only to one university at a time for second university please fill the form again · Seats would be filled on first in-first out basis and are fully at the discretion of selection committee at LPU & partner University · There can be possibility of online, offline or hybrid classes by the partner university. For further information please contact Division of International Affairs at studyabroad@lpu.co.in

title: Opportunity to participate in International level Essay Writing competition : (3/2/2021)
body: LPU Literary Society under the aegis of Department of Cultural Affairs, DSW invited entries for an International Level online essay writing competition on topic 'Veda for World Peace' . Any person born after 1990 can participate . The participation and registration is free. Interested participants are advised to send email your essay at Vaishali.23510@lpu.co.in by 6th March, 2021 Winners will be awarded with handsome cash prizes. Participation certificate will also be provided by the organizers. Rules and regulations- 1. Language: English /Hindi /Sanskrit 2. .All the essays will be judged on the basis of logic, survey, writing style, innovation, structure, etc. 3. We appreciate simple ideas but always discourage copied content even though it looks attractive. 4. We will not judge copied essays and it will be rejected during the screening process only and no certificate will be issued. Registration: No registration fee required- The essay should be minimum 750 words and maximum 3000 words.- The submitted essay should be plagiarism free. Plagiarized essay will not be accepted for the contest.- Participants should write their Name, DOB, Category: School/College/University, City, Phone number, E-mail ID, and Photo (optional) in your entry at the very beginning before start writing the essay.- Participants are encouraged to write in passive voice. Avoid writing “I” or personal experiences unless the topic is such that you are compelled to write your experience.- The decision of jury member is the FINAL and no queries related to result will be entertained- No essay would be entertained after the deadline for submission.- The essay should be typed in MS word format and pdf copy should be mailed. Awards:- The essays will be grouped as First, Second, Third, Editor’s Choice Essay, Praiseworthy and Worth Mentioning according to the marks given by the judges to each of the essays. Apart from this a large number of consolation prizes will be given. First Prize -Rs 75,000 Second Prize- Rs 50,000 Third Prize- Rs 25,000 Editors Choice, Praise worthy and Worth mentioning essay : 5000 Consolation 10 Prize- Rs 1000 each For queries - contact Ms Vaishali(7009747963)

title: Did You Know? Central Library Subscribes EPWRF India Time Series : (3/2/2021)
body: EPWRF India Time Series is a unique online database with its comprehensive coverage of Indian economy for a fairly long time period and it comprises over 50,000 variables capsuled in 20 modules. The database tries to provide in continuous time series from 1950 depending on the availability. The database is well accepted by the research community in India as well as abroad. Major subscribers include several Indian Council of Social Science Research (ICSSR) institutes and Universities (central, state and private), IIMs, IITs, Banks and top-ranked management institutes. Some of the prominent modules are given below: • National Account Statistics of India • Domestic products of States of India • Agricultural Statistics • Wage rates in rural India • India production series • Statistics of Mines • Price indices • Annual survey of Industries • Industrial Production Series • Health statistics • Insurance statistics • Educational statistics • Health Statistics • Financial markets • Banking statistics You all are encouraged to extensively use this resource for research and academic purposes. Way to access EPWRF India Times Series: UMS Navigation-->Library --->E-resources--> http://ezproxy.lpu.in/menu Enter UMS credentials and start accessing all the resources OR Visit: http://ezproxy.lpu.in/ -->Enter UMS username/password -->Databases--->EPWRF India Times Series For further queries kindly contact Dr. Jatinder Kumar (University Librarian). title: Want to talk about your problems and learn to deal with issues of stress, anxiety, anger , relationships and overthinking ? Join an interactive session with Counseling Psychologists on Wednesday 3rd March 2021. (Ref. No. LPU/DSR/IC/210302/001) : (3/2/2021)
body: Dear Students If You’ve got Problems, We’ve got Ears. During this Pandemic some of you may be overthinking, feeling lonely and going through emotions of frustration, anger, stress, sadness and relationship issues. Avoiding emotions affect your body and mind. It can lead to problems with memory and concentration due to stress and anxiety In LPU we endeavour to strive towards better student mental health and psychological well-being which are important to a student’s success and confidence. Talking about your problems can release pent-up feelings Don't suffer alone, come and talk to trained professionals about your concerns . We can help you find new ideas in order to move forward. title: Equality Hackathon : (3/1/2021)
body: For more than a century, people around the world have celebrated International Women’s Day on March 8th. It’s a day to focus on the achievements of women, and continue the fight for global equality. Student Research and Project Cell under the aegis of Division of Student Welfare is upcoming with an event titled “Equality Hackathon” to celebrate the Women’s Day. This event will provide opportunity to students to pitch their innovative solutions for some real life issues facing by the women of our country.The best ideas will incubated by SRPC and also rewarded with some exciting prizes. There are Four Tracks: Health: Hack a solution that will help women access health and hygiene resources Physical Safety: Hack a solution that advances women’s physical safety Psychological Safety: Hack a solution that advances women's psychological safety Financial Safety: Hack a solution that will empower women financially. Note: The solution could be a product, a service, or a business idea. Each team needs to identify only “one” track. Round 1: Prelims - Online Solution Submission 1) Submission of Idea via mail @mandeep.16853@lpu.co.in. 2) The team will need to mention the track that they wish to apply to in the document. Round 2: Idea Presentation 1) The teams will have to give a maximum 10 min presentation which includes team member details, possible solution, implementation plan, and the cost. 2) The presentation will be followed by Q&A session Last Date of Submission of Idea :8th March 2021 Event Day: 9th Mar,2021, 5:30 pm -7:30 pm Registration Link: http://tiny.cc/equalityhack Note: The idea should be submitted in PDF format and the document must comprise of name and registration number Prizes: Top 3 teams will be awarded with exciting prizes and certificate of Merit.The top 3 ideas will be incubated under SRPC-DSW . Certificate will be provided to all the participants
uploaded_by: Attachment: 1 Equality Hack.png Uploaded By: Office of HOD Division of Student Services *This is computer generated notice, not requiring signature

title: Faces For Equality : (3/1/2021)
body: On March 8,International Women’s Day ,Student Research and Project Cell, DSW is giving you the opportunity to speak up about gender discrimination against women. Participants can send in short writings with their own experiences and thoughts on gender bias. The writings can be about current socio-political inequalities women face or their own personal thoughts and experiences on how women are treated differently in today’s society. Imagine yourself in the shoes of the opposite gender and write about the things you could have done differently to attain gender equality. There is only one round. 1)Only the writing sent to the mail provided will be considered for evaluation. 2)Entries that are not genuine/created on multiple blogs purely for claiming prizes will be rejected. Judge's decision on the winners is final. 3)Maximum number of words: (500 max.) Register at: http://tiny.cc/faces4equality Submit your article @ hiteshagarwal135h@gmail.com Last Dtae of Submission 7th March 2021 The idea should be submitted in a PDF format The file must possess your name and Registration No Best Article will be awarded with Certificate of Merit and Exciting prizes.The article will also be published on various official social platform of SRPC AND DSW Certificates will be provided to all the participants.
uploaded_by: Attachment: 1 FACES For Equality.png Uploaded By: Office of HOD Division of Student Services *This is computer generated notice, not requiring signature

title: Session on “E-waste Management in India” (LPU/DII/IC/210226/001) : (2/26/2021)
body: Dear All, Division of Industry Interface in collaboration with Centre for Science and Environment has brought a wonderful opportunity of a virtual session on “E-waste Management in India”. With the explosive growth in use of electrical and electronic equipment, generation of e-waste and its management has emerged as a formidable challenge. The UN has referred to this phenomenon as a “tsunami” of e-waste. While e-waste is a problem, it can easily be moulded into a solution. It is the most valuable of wastes, as it contains many rare and precious metals and materials. Speakers: 1) Dr. Rachna Arora- Team leader & Coordinator EU- Resource Efficiency Initiative India. 2) Dr. Sandeep Chatterjee- Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology, Government of India. 3) Dr. Deepali Sinha – Managing Director Sofias Sustainability Leaders Pvt. Ltd. 4) Pranshu Singhal- Founder, Karo Sambhav. 5) Siddharth Ghanshyam Singh- Deputy Programme Manager, Solid Waste Management Unit Centre for Science and Environment. 6) Atin Biswas- Programme Director , Solid Waste management Unit , Centre for Science and Environment. Date: February 26, 2021 ( Friday) Time - 2:00 PM to 3:30 PM Link for registration: https://tinyurl.com/t5aujdwn For more details Please contact Ms. Neha Bhatija , Division of Industry Interface at neha.24499@lpu.co.in

title: Equality Hackathon : (2/25/2021)
body: For more than a century, people around the world have celebrated International Women’s Day on March 8th. It’s a day to focus on the achievements of women, and continue the fight for global equality. Student Research and Project Cell under the aegis of Division of Student Welfare is upcoming with an event titled “Equality Hackathon” to celebrate the Women’s Day. This event will provide opportunity to students to pitch their innovative solutions for some real life issues facing by the women of our country.The best ideas will incubated by SRPC and also rewarded with some exciting prizes. There are Four Tracks: Health: Hack a solution that will help women access health and hygiene resources Physical Safety: Hack a solution that advances women’s physical safety Psychological Safety: Hack a solution that advances women's psychological safety Financial Safety: Hack a solution that will empower women financially Note: 1)The solution could be a product, a service, or a business idea. 2)Each team needs to identify only “one” track. Round 1: Prelims - Online Solution Submission 1) Submission of Idea via mail @mandeep.16853@lpu.co.in. 2) The team will need to mention the track that they wish to apply to in the document. Round 2: Idea Presentation 1) The teams will have to give a maximum 10 min presentation which includes team member details, possible solution, implementation plan, and the cost. 2) The presentation will be followed by Q&A session Last Date of Submission of Idea :8th March 2021 Event Day: 9th Mar,2021, 5:30 pm -7:30 pm Registration Link: http://tiny.cc/equalityhack Top 3 ideas will get exciting prizes and Certificate of Merit.The top ideas will be incubated by SRPC for prototyping . Certificates will be provided to the participants.

title: Design For Girls education : A Poster making Competition : (2/25/2021)
body: Without achieving gender equality for girls in education, the world has no chance of achieving many of the ambitious health, social and development targets it has set for itself. title: SIGNS OF STRESS: Worth Discussing with a Counselor Shared by psychologists from Counseling & happiness cell. (Ref. No. LPU/DSR/IC/210224/001) : (2/24/2021)
body: Dear Students “Stress is caused by being ‘here' but wanting to be ‘there.' - Eckhart Tolle “If the problem can be solved why worry? If the problem cannot be solved worrying will do you no good.” - Shantideva We all have been stressed at some point in our lives. Stress is the cause of many illnesses. We need to recognize Psychological and emotional signs of stress to avoid these illnesses. . Feeling unmotivated, or unfocused. . Anger, irritability. . Trouble sleeping or sleeping too much. . Racing thoughts or constant worry. . Problems with your memory or concentration. . Lack of decision-making However, it’s seen that people don't talk about their problems and suffer in silence. · Studies have shown that simply talking about our problems and sharing our negative emotions with someone we trust can be profoundly healing- reducing stress, strengthening our immune system, and reducing physical and emotional distress. Psychologists from counseling & happiness cell - share tips to help students recognize the signs of stress and consult expert psychologists to live a happy and healthy life. We care about your emotional and psychological well-being. Please email us – counseling.happiness@lpu.co.in PFA – Signs of stress: Worth discussing with a Counselor Attachment: Signs of stress

title: Want to talk about your problems and learn to deal with issues of stress, anxiety, anger , relationships and overthinking ? Join an interactive session with Counseling Psychologists on Wednesday 24th February 2021. (Ref. No. LPU/DSR/IC/210222/001) : (2/22/2021)
body: Dear Students If You’ve got Problems, We’ve got Ears. During this Pandemic some of you may be overthinking, feeling lonely and going through emotions of frustration, anger, stress, sadness and relationship issues. It can lead to problems with memory and concentration due to stress and anxiety In LPU we endeavour to strive towards better student mental health and psychological well-being which are important to a student’s success and confidence. title: Allotment of Residential Facilities (March-May 2021) For Offline Class Optees : (2/20/2021)
body: Online Allotment Process for Residential Facilities i.e. Residence, Mess, Laundry, Vehicle Parking, Gym, Sports facility for term-II (Session 2020-21) is being started. Allotment of residence will be done as per the guidelines of UGC, Govt. of Punjab and Ministry of health and family welfare (GOI). The residence facility can be booked as an INDIVIDUAL or as a GROUP (in which more than one student opt for same room) through hostel booking interface in UMS Dashboard. Only those students who are going to attend offline classes in session 2020-21 will be eligible to participate in Allotment process and book residential facilities. Allotment will be separately managed for students awarded hostel fee waiver under any scholarship scheme (like Sports, Cultural, Board topper etc.) and those who have already booked residential facility for session 2020-21, such students need not to participate in the Allotment Process of Residential Facilities. The “Allotment Process of Residential Facilities’’ is three-step process as detailed below: Step 1: Registration for Participating in Allotment Process - Eligible students will be required to register by paying a non-refundable registration fee of Rs. 1000. However the registration fee of Rs. 1000/- will be adjusted in charges for residential facilities. Step 2: Provisional Booking of Residential Facilities - All the registered students can select and provisionally book the desired hostel building, seater and room along with other residential facilities e.g. Mess, Laundry, Vehicle parking, Gym, Sports facility (swimming will not be the part of sports facility booking). - Student can change his/her preference/provisional booking multiple times subject to availability of the room/seater before the last date of provisional booking (as mentioned in table below). The preference recorded at 11.59PM on last date will be considered final. Step 3: Confirmation of Allotment by Payment of Charges for Residential Facilities - The charges for selected residential facilities will be debited in student’s account to be paid by due date, failing which the late payment charges may be applicable. - The charges of residential facilities can be paid using one of the following modes: o Through University website using Credit card / Debit Card / Net Banking / UPI o PayTM App. o Demand Draft drawn in favour of LOVELY FACILITIES payable at JALANDHAR. o Cash payment in University campus (Block 32, Level 1) Important Dates Activity Start Date End Date Register for Participation in Allotment Process 21 Feb. 2021 12:00 PM 25 Feb. 2021 11:59 PM Provisional Booking 21 Feb. 2021 12:00 PM 25 Feb. 2021 11:59 PM Charges Debiting in Student’s Account 26 Feb. 2021 26 Feb. 2021 Hostels Opening for Stay 01 Mar. 2021 - Date of Depositing Charges (without late charges) Before reporting in University or 05th Mar. 2021, whichever is earlier. - Spl. Benefits:- In this time of uncertainty due to pandemic, as a hand of support to the students following 02 options of special benefits have been given to opt. from: 1. Students can pre-book the hostel seat for coming session 2021-22 along with booking for the duration March to May 2021 (i.e. Booking for 13 months). In this case, initially student has to pay the charges for 03 months (March to May 2021) from which 02 months charges will be adjusted in coming session hostel charges (10 months charges). Adjustment will be applicable for Hostel, Gym, Sports and Parking charges only for the said duration. Student has to pay Mess charges, Laundry charges and Electricity charges (as per consumption over and above the allocated free units @ applicable rate). 2. Students can pre-book the hostel seat for summer vacations and coming session 2021-22 along with booking for the duration March to May 2021 (i.e. Booking for 15 months). In this case, initially student has to pay the charges for 03 months (March to May 2021) which will be adjusted in coming session hostel charges (12 months charges). Adjustment will be applicable for Hostel, Gym, Sports and Parking charges only for the said duration. Student has to pay Mess charges, Laundry charges and Electricity charges (as per consumption over and above the allocated free units @ applicable rate). In case any student wants to cancel the facility afterward he/she has to pay the complete charges for the duration March-May 2021. For any query contact on: Mob. 62830-52138, 98782-62519 (between 09 AM to 05 PM) Note:- 1. To maintain social distancing students can avail only 01 seater to 04 seater (Except the students who have already been allocated accommodation in hostels, in these cases the booked seater will be as it is but the room capacity may be adjusted wherever needed). 2. Students who have already booked residential facility for the session 2020-21 can also avail the benefit of booking for 15 months through the hostel booking interface in UMS. 3. In case after booking, university is constrained to stop any facility (due to any unforeseen reason) charge debited against that facility will be adjusted in student fee account. 4. For online booking, Boys Hostel-01 & Boys Hostel-02 will be opened for male students (Boys Hostel-02 will be opened once 90% of the available seats in Boys Hostel-01 will be booked). Girls Hostel-05 & Girls Hostel-06 will be opened for Female students. The above announcement should be read along with following Enclosures. 1. Charges for Residential Facilities 2. General Guidelines. 3. How to use UMS for two step Allotment process.

title: Important information regarding offline classes and examination schedule for term 20212. (Ref. No. LPU/DAA/IC/210218/001) : (2/18/2021)
body: In order to ensure that the academic progress of the students is continued in a smooth manner and in compliance with the guidelines issued by regulatory bodies and state/central government, the University is planning to extend the option of offline classes for all the students. In this regard, the students are advised to carefully go through the below mentioned important points: 1. The offline classes for the students who have submitted consent to attend classes in the offline mode at University Campus, shall commence after the Mid Term Test. The student shall be required to report on University Campus with their RTPCR test report within maximum of 10 days from the last MTT exam date. 2. Mid Term Test shall be conducted in online mode for all the students. 3. Duty leave shall be provided to student to facilitate their travel. The students must make prior bookings/travel arrangements so that they report on Campus by the reporting date. However, the students should plan their travel dates after their Mid Term Test. No exemption in MTT shall be given against travel. 4. For the students interested to avail University hostel facility, information regarding the booking procedure shall be informed shortly. 5. Only the students who have given consent for attending the classes in offline mode can report in the University for the offline classes. 6. The students who selected “Online Mode” as the preferred mode of attending classes/who have not selected any option for the mode of attending classes, shall continue attending their online classes from their hometowns. Their attendance shall be recorded only via online MyClass platform. 7. However, in case of any exigency, any student who has submitted consent for offline classes cannot make the required travel arrangements or is unwilling/unable to report in the University for the purpose now, then he/she shall also be allowed to continue attending the online classes from his/her hometown and his/her attendance shall be also be recorded via MyClass platform. 8. The End Term Examination for term 20212 shall be conducted in OFFLINE mode in a phased manner for all the students. 9. Every student shall have a dedicated slot for the conduct of ETE-20212 and the student wise individual examination slot shall be displayed in the UMS seating plan at least one month before the start date of examination. 10. The students who shall be attending the classes of term 20212 in the online mode, should plan their travel arrangements only after viewing their individual ETE slots. The ETE slots may vary for students, hence refrain from making any travel bookings until your ETE slot is displayed in your UMS. 11. Students should note that once they report on Campus, their movement in and out of the University shall be restricted in view of COVID-19 safety precautions and it shall be compulsory for the students to abide by all the guidelines prescribed by the University. 12. The students shall be mandatorily required to take all precautions and maintain personal hygiene; hence they should wear face masks/covers on Campus; and carry masks/sanitizers with them every time. 13. The students shall be compulsorily required to submit the filled hard copy of the undertaking form (attached with the communication) upon reporting in University.

title: Schedule for Online Test of JOSH TECHNOLOGY GROUP (TC.2946.2022.18644) : (2/14/2021)
body: This is for the information of all the concerned that the online test for the shortlisted students (as per attached list) of JOSH TECHNOLOGY GROUP (TC.2946.2022.18644) is scheduled as follows: Date: 15-02-2021 Test Time for Software Developer: 10 AM Objective Test Duration: 50 minutes Subjective Test Time: 2:00 PM Subjective Test Duration: 75 minutes Test Time for Front End Developer: 12 Noon Objective Test Duration: 60 minutes Subjective Test Time: 4:30 PM Subjective Test Duration: 75 minutes NOTE: Students who clear the first Objective Test will only be eligible for the Second Subjective Round. Here are the Prerequisites for the Online Test that the students have to follow : An online test link on the registered email id will be sent to you a day before the scheduled date via 'Calyxpod' however the test will start only at the scheduled time for the respective tests. (Please check your Inbox/Spam for the email) A laptop/desktop with an active web camera and mobile phone with front camera is mandatory to take the test.Though laptop/desktop is advisable. Location and Webcam permission is mandatory. You will be proctored throughout the test. Please ensure that you are logged out from all the QT and Online Test Sessions otherwise your test will not run. The test will not run on Windows 7. If you are not able to start the test through any of the above mentioned ways, please take the test on your mobile phone through Google Chrome. The test runs on any Modern browser however, Google Chrome Browser is recommended as it is a light browser. Please download the same or update your existing browser. The test will not run on Mozilla Firefox. If you connect with the broadband, a minimum internet speed required is 512 Kbps and data speed required is minimum 3G for mobile. However, 1 Mbps and above is desired. You should have data of at least 200 MB in order to take the test. If you are taking multiple tests, 1 GB data is advisable. You are advised to keep all the browsers, device apps or notifications disabled during the test. It will help you to get the optimum speed of the internet. Keeping other browsers or apps open or switching to any other tab during the test may lead to violations and the test will be terminated. Once the duration of the test is over the test will automatically stop. It will be a purely technical test based on the technical framework. Please refer to the job description for more details. You should use the same email address to take the test on which they will receive the test link. You are advised to read the instructions carefully before starting the test. You should be logged in 15 mins before the test scheduled time. Instructions for the Subjective Test of Software Developer: Students who clear the first Objective Test for Software Developer will only be eligible for the Second Subjective Round and get the link. You need to write the complete code. Just the description, or the Pseudo Code will not be given any marks. Function Signature is provided in the Questions. You can choose a different function signature if they want but they need to specify the reason for the same. You need not write the main function or take any input from the user or output anything on the screen. You just need to write the required function. You are advised to go through their code properly to ensure that all the edge cases / corner cases are handled. Marks will be deducted if edge cases are not handled properly.You can code in either C, C++ or JAVA only. You are not allowed to use any high level inbuilt functions for searching, sorting, linked lists, Trees, ArrayLists etc. You need to specify some comments in the code or describe the approach / algorithm. Same will help the evaluator in understanding the code better. Please do all the checks recommended in the system & connectivity test link, once today & again half an hour before the test. This will lead to facing lesser issues during the test. If you're unable to view the questions in the test, you are advised to follow the below mentioned steps: a) Try to refresh the page. b) If refreshing doesn't help, please clear the browser, close the test & click on the test URL again. Please don't click on Finish the test. Finding a solution once you have ended the test would not be possible. Students are requested to wear appropriate clothes while taking the test and their webcam should be in working condition.

title: Webinar on IPR on 19th Feb 2021 : (2/9/2021)
body: Launched in July 2018, IPTSE is the first & one-of- its-kind annual ‘IP Olympiad’ for Intellectual Property Rights in India that tests the knowledge of an individual on patents, designs, copyright, designs, geographical indications and trade secret. IPTSE is supported by several organizations that believe in knowledge-based economy such as ASSOCHAM, ERICSSON, and different Government bodies. Pls see the attachment “About IPTSE rewards & Benefits”. For details please visit https://iptse.com/. Role of Intellectual Property cannot be underestimated as it helps in inclusive growth. There are several initiatives take by different government bodies in the realm of IP such as MHRD launched innovation cells for higher education institutes; CIPAM’s IP outreach activities; reimbursement programs for Indian innovators filing IP by Miety, UGC and AICTE recommendation to incorporate IPRs in the curriculum etc. Hence, there is an immense need to create awareness about IP and IPRs among faculty, scientists, researchers and students about identification, protection, management and commercialization of IP. In the above backdrop, IPTSE team is pleased to organize a free IP webinar on the topic of “Role of Intellectual Property in Career Building”. Dr Sheetal Chopra, Course Director IPTSE & Director IPR Policy, Ericsson will be speaking on this topic. Those interested may like to register using registration link: https://forms.gle/79XtaSz9Ueaydteq6 Registration link will be open until 17th Feb. Joining link will be shared with the registrants on 18th Feb.

General Instructions:- 1. A laptop with a functional webcam is mandatory. 2. The candidates need to take the test on a computer/laptop system, equipped with a working Web-Cam (external or built-in) and smooth internet connectivity throughout the test session. 3. Candidates are advised to take the test in all fair means. 4. Candidates are advised that if the link is not working by clicking on it then kindly copy and paste the link to the different browsers. 5. It should not be covered with any object and should always have the candidate right in front of it. 7. While taking up the online test, candidates are advised not to move out of the test screen, e.g., Do not open another tab or application like notepad, excel or web browsers.

title: Webinar on “ Innovations and advances in somatic cell nuclear transfer of farm animals" : (2/1/2021)
body: Successful cloning of monkeys, the first non-human primate species, by somatic cell nuclear transfer (SCNT) attracted worldwide attention in 2018. Remarkably, it has taken more than 20 years since the cloning of Dolly the sheep in 1997 to achieve this feat. This success was largely due to recent understanding of epigenetic barriers that impede SCNT-mediated reprogramming and the establishment of key methods to overcome these barriers, which also allowed efficient derivation of human pluripotent stem cells for cell therapy. Division of Innovation and Entrepreneurship brings you an amazing webinar on “ Innovations and advances in somatic cell nuclear transfer of farm animals”. In this webinar our guest speaker Dr. Naresh Selokar will discuss recent advances in SCNT technology and its potential applications for both reproductive and therapeutic cloning. body: Dear Students , ASK YOURSELF Do you fume and fret , feel frustrated, irritable, testy , touchy, offended, easily upset and easily angered ? Do you show aggressive behavior , get violent and angry often ? Do you get easily annoyed or bothered, and show snappish behavior? Do you start shouting, throwing things around , get angry on small things ? Anger is a known symptom of several mental health conditions. title: Regarding NSRCEL, the Statup Hub : (1/28/2021)
body: NSRCEL, the startup hub at IIM Bangalore, is collaborating with Capgemini in India to support social startups under the NSRCEL Social program. The program aims to support not-for-profit tech enabled ventures solving social problems and impacting areas of Education, Employability and Environment. The program will be accepting applications from January 6, 2021 onwards. Early-stage ventures (not older than two years with a minimum of six months of groundwork) will be shortlisted for a three-month long pre-incubation phase of the program. During the pre-incubation phase, entrepreneurs will be engaged in capacity-building workshops and sessions by sector- specific experts to enrich their technical know-how. The entrepreneurs will get a robust opportunity to network with 800+ ventures from previous cohorts at NSRCEL. Program Highlights: • Curated Mentors • Industry Connects • Opportunity to pitch for Incubation • Funding support of up to Rs. 20 Lakhs Last Date to apply: February 15, 2021 Follow the link: - https://www.nsrcel.org/ For any Entrepreneurial Mentorship and Guidance, contact Dr. Kanishka Jha, Block-13, Room 208, Cabin-2 or write to kanishka.21537@lpu.co.in +91 79872 26635

title: EAT THE FROG – It works – Best time management method Shared by psychologists from Counseling & happiness cell. (Ref. No. LPU/DSR/IC/210128/001) : (1/28/2021)
body: Dear Students , Brian Tracy the famous Canadian-American motivational public speaker and self-development author promotes the theory of - Eat That Frog!, No Excuses! Don't panic, eating a frog is obviously a metaphor. It was devised by Brian Tracy, who wrote the book ‘Eat That Frog! 21 Great Ways to Stop Procrastinating and Get More Done in Less Time’. Mark Twain once said that if the first thing you do each morning is to eat a live frog, you can go through the day with the satisfaction of knowing that that is probably the worst thing that is going to happen to you all day long. Psychologists from counseling & happiness cell – share tips from this book to help students learn this time management technique . We care about your emotional and psychological well being . Please email us – counseling.happiness@lpu.co.in PFA – EAT THE FROG – Tips to overcome procrastination Attachment : Eat the frog

Students have to serve at least one person who needs food, or some clothes, or anything else in the nearby area of their locality this Republic Day. Let come together and assure that this Republic Day no person sleeps with an empty stomach. Once a person completes his task of helping someone in their locality then they can ask their friends to do the same with at least one person in their locality so that we can build a chain and serve the needy. title: Registration for Backlog Courses for Spring Term, 2020-21 (Ref. No. LPU/DOE/IC/210113/001) : (1/13/2021)
body: To facilitate the students to clear the backlog courses in the regular current term (Spring Term) the registration for backlog courses has been started for Spring Term of Academic Session, 2020-21. The platform for registration for backlog courses is open now. However, before registration of the courses the students must understand the below stated points: a. The time table for courses running in Second Year and onwards has already been locked whereas the time table for courses to be offered in First Year shall be locked by January 21st, 2021. b. The students who have to register for only courses which are being offered in Second Year or onwards should immediately register for the same after due verification of the time table (as the time table for these courses is locked). The students should register for these courses latest by January 20th, 2021. c. The students who have to register for courses being offered only in First Year should register after January 21st, 2021 after the Time Table of these courses is locked. d. The students who have to register for a mix of courses to be offered in First Year and in Second Year and onwards can also register their final choice of courses after January 21st, 2021 onwards so that there are no clashes in the Time Table of courses being registered. The last date for registration in this case shall be January 25th, 2021. Find below important guidelines for the Registration Process of the same. 1. Link to be followed for registration of backlog courses: UMS Navigation→ Examination system→ Backlog Registration → Backlog Course Registration You can register the backlog courses through LPU Touch as well. After logging in LPU Touch, open the side menu and go to Backlog Registration. (Screen shot attached for your reference). 2. Further in the upcoming term (Spring Term), the students may also opt for Grade conversion. The permissibility of grade conversions shall be as per the table given below: S. No. Existing grade New Grade Conversion 1. E G Allowed 2. E F Allowed 3. G F Allowed 3. Conditions applicable for backlog registration: A. For Continuing students: In addition to the courses for the current regular term of the student shall be allowed to register in backlog courses if the student has minimum 2.5 CGPA or 25% cumulative mark percentage (in case of marks based programme). i. If a student wants to register for only F grade courses, then he/she can register for maximum of four F grade courses subject to availability of clash-free time table schedule. However, the student may request for registration of an extra course which has been offered in this term by sending the email at academic.aac@lpu.co.in during the time of registration. ii. If a student wants to register only G grade courses, then he/she can register for maximum of nine G grade courses. iii. A student wants to register both F and G grade courses, he/she can register maximum of nine courses of which maximum of four F grade courses can be registered subject to availability of clash-free time table schedule. B. For Non-Promoted students: A student, who is registering only for backlog courses because of the non-promotion to the next year, the student can register for a maximum of 9 courses subject to availability of clash-free time table schedule. If a student has studied more than 9 courses in a single term then student may apply for additional backlog courses in the term by sending the email at academic.aac@lpu.co.in during the time of registration. C. Registration in a course for additional courses/courses not mapped/not studied by student: A student who is registering for additional courses/courses not mapped/not studied by the students due to Change of Program, Term off/Year off, Re-joining after gap or Migration is marked as “M” grade in result. Student will be required to register the course(s) as F grade. “M” Grade cannot be converted to G grade. 4. Fee for backlog registration: The student Registration will be confirmed subject to payment of the backlog fee. The backlog fee shall be payable online through the fee payment gateway i. For National Students including “Asia”: Backlog registration fee for a course shall be 1/10th of the student’s standard tuition fee plus Rs.350/- as examination fee and should be paid at time of registration through online mode only. ii. For International Students: Backlog registration fee for a course shall be 1/10thof the student’s standard tuition fee and USD 7 as examination fee and should be paid within 48 hours through University Website as per link:: https://www.lpu.in/frmloginaccounts.aspx iii. For scholarship holders or students for whom the fee has been waived off (fully or partly) by the University, the backlog fee will be 1/10th of the actual or standard tuition fee for the term and not the fee after scholarship or waiver. iv. For students admitted to dual and / or integrated programmes, the backlog fee shall be charged after considering whether it pertains to the lower degree or the higher degree. v. In case a student’s batch has graduated or passed out, the backlog registration fee for a course shall be 1/10th of the student’s standard tuition fee of the programme. vi. For term off and non-promoted students: Backlog fee will be 1/10 of his/her fellow batch’s fee until his/her fellow batch student is studying that program. Backlog fee will be 1/10 of the last term fee paid by his/her fellow batch in case the batch has passed out. vii. Once student has paid the backlog courses fee, courses cannot be De-registered. 5. Attendance Marking: i. Attendance will be counted from very next day of your registration confirmation i.e. after confirmation of your fee payment. ii. Attendance in backlog courses will be included in the aggregate attendance of the student for the purpose of determining his/her eligibility for appearing in the ETE and for calculating the detention list. 6. Equivalency of Courses: i. Students are required to ensure that the equivalent course allotted to them have not been previously studied by them. If equivalence course has already been studied by them, then they are required to report the same immediately by sending the email at academic.aac@lpu.co.in ii. Also, for equivalent courses, the credits of the new course will be applicable. 7. Step by Step guide for using the interface for backlog registration is attached along with these guidelines.

body: This is for the information of all the concerned that the Online test for registered students of PROLIFICS CORPORATION LTD INDIA (OC.10113.2021.18451) is scheduled as follows: Test Date : 13-01-2021 Test Time : 09 : 00 AM - 09 : 00 PM Test Duration : 1 hour 30 Minutes NOTE: Test link will be shared in the registered email ids of the students by the company. Procedure to take the test: 1. The candidate needs to login to the MATCH platform and sign in with the registered email id 2.Password, Post successful login. 3. Click to the profile to update your details. 4.Go to the Events section and click and proceed to appear for the online test which will open in a new tab. 5. You will be redirected to the online test page, read the instructions carefully and click on the proceed to appear for the online test. Candidate Requirements & Guidelines : Technical Requirements: a) Functional Computer systems with seamless Internet Connectivity b) Windows Operating System (No other Operating System is supported). c) Min. 1 MBPS internet speed per PC. d) Updated Google Chrome or Mozilla Firefox Browser with the most recent version; Note: IE is not supported. e) Web Cam is mandatory to take the test. Don’ts: For Candidates : a) Candidate should not move or go outside the test window as they will be marked suspicious and if tried to do so repeatedly the test may get terminated. b) Candidates are not allowed to use any mobile phones or Calculators during the test process. c) Keep the webcam ON in your PC/Laptop. d) The test is monitored and has strong proctoring mechanisms, hence advised not to cheat in any manner.

title: LPU Global: Info-Sessions for Credit transfer and Semester Abroad Program for LPU students. : (1/11/2021)
body: Division of International Affairs brings great opportunity for the students of Lovely Professional University to have an international exposure through programs like credit transfer and semester abroad program. Here is the brief synopsis of both the programs being offered by the Division of International Affairs to the students of Lovely Professional University 1. Credit Transfer Program: We offer the students to get an international degree by taking the option of Credit Transfer. Under this opportunity student can study 2/2.5 years at LPU and complete the rest of his/her degree at a foreign university and get a degree from the partner University after successful completion of the program at the partner university. Credit transfer is the process by which one institution matches its courses or requirements to course work at another institution. Credits earned at LPU can be transferred to the host University. Students use credit transfer to assure that courses they complete will not have to be repeated at the institution to which they are transferring. 2. Semester Abroad: Under Semester exchange student spends a full semester at partner foreign university. After studying for a semester at a Partner University the student gets his/her credits transferred back to LPU. A semester at a partner university can be of two types: · Scholarship Semester Abroad · Paid Semester Abroad Under tuition fee waived semester the student pays only the tuition fees of the home university and does not pay tuition fees of the host university. Under tuition paid semester the student pays tuition fee of the home as well as Host University. This opportunity can be availed by the student who has completed one year of study at home university. Other expenses relating to VISA, Accommodation (where applicable), food, and any other charges of home or host institute has to borne by the student. The interested students can interact with representative of Division of International Affairs on one to one basis and get their queries solved on your preferred date as per the schedule provided below in the table Date Time Topic of Session Link to register for the session 21/01/2021 4 PM to 5 PM Credit Transfer https://forms.gle/vnY9Cu2GFX2xNxPk8 22/01/2021 4 PM to 5 PM Semester Abroad https://forms.gle/9njMNX932duSnF8BA For further information please contact Division of International Affairs at studyabroad@lpu.co.in

title: FREE counseling Sessions - Connect with Psychologists from Counseling & Happiness Cell. (Ref. No. LPU/DSR/IC/210109/003) : (1/9/2021)
body: Dear Students, For us Mental health and wellbeing of all LPU community is very important. Sometimes in our lives, some of us face emotional and psychological challenges. We need to recognize Psychological and emotional signs of stress: . Anger, irritability, or restlessness, Anxiety . Feeling overwhelmed, unmotivated, or unfocused. . Trouble sleeping or sleeping too much. . Racing thoughts or constant worry. Overthinking. . Problems with your memory or concentration. . Making bad decisions. However, it’s seen that people don't talk about their problems and suffer in silence. · Studies have shown that simply talking about our problems and sharing our negative emotions with someone we trust can be profoundly healing—reducing stress, strengthening our immune system, and reducing physical and emotional distress . Talking about your problems can release pent-up feelings. . Talking to someone outside of the situation may help you to find a solution to the problem. . If you don't think you can discuss the problem with anyone you know, You can share your emotional, psychological and behavioral concerns with the counseling psychologists, who will help you deal with your concerns, empathically. All counseling sessions are free and confidentiality of your interaction is strictly maintained. Students and staff residing in the Hostels can contact their wardens who will help you get through to us Or Email us – counseling.happiness@lpu.co.in and our Psychologist will get in touch to arrange a session. Please mention your Name, Registration number and Contact phone number.

title: Updations in the RMS Interface. (Ref. No. LPU/DSR/IC/210901/001) : (1/9/2021)
body: Division of Student Relationship is looking forward to make the student grievance/request system more swift and effective. In order to do that, Relationship Management System (RMS) has been updated with new features that help us to serve you in a better manner. All the students are advised to log RMS for their queries/request/grievance/suggestion etc. The updations in RMS are as follows: 1. Attachment of Documents: While lodging the RMS, a provision is being provided to attach the supporting documents. It will help the Dealing Official to understand and authenticate your request in a better manner and it will be easy to process your request. (If you have multiple documents to attach then it is suggested merge them all and make a compiled(single) file and then upload it) 2. In Process: When your request is under consideration then you will receive a UMS My Message that “Your request of ticket number…….has been received and it is in process.” 3. Two way communication: Dealing official can ask you the additional information about your logged RMS and that will be visible in your “UMS My Message”. You are advised to provide the asked information in the same RMS (as it remains open). 4. Providing Rating on the Reply: Once the RMS is closed by Dealing Official then Student can rate the reply of Dealing Official on a scale of 1 to5. Where “1” being Highly Unsatisfactory and “5” Being Highly Satisfactory. These rating remarks will help us to provide you the better solution of the same query. Unsatisfactory rating will escalate the RMS to highe­­­­­­­­r level and you will be provided the better assistance in such case. Mechanism to Log on to RMS: UMS Navigation --> Relationship Management System --> Log Request--->Message Type-- > Category Type -- > Department -- > Category -- > Sub Category -- > Contact No. -- > Description. title: Registration for Ph.D. End Term Presentation (ETP). (Ref. No. LPU/DOE/IC/210105/003) : (1/5/2021)
body: This is in reference to the Ph.D. End Term Presentation (ETP) evaluation which shall be tentatively scheduled from February 2021 onwards (exact dates will be shared in due course of time). All the research scholars who have registered for their respective Ph.D. programs after July 2016 and have successfully completed their State of the Art Seminar (SAS) evaluation are required to appear for End Term Presentation (ETP) after each 6 months from the date of successful completion of SAS. The main aim of the End Term Presentation is as follows: a. To present the action taken against the recommendations given by the Research Advisory Committee (RAC) in the last evaluation. b. Justification in case a particular suggestion is not incorporated c. To present amount of work done or progress made since last evaluation The research scholars are required to follow the following two steps for appearing in ETP: Step-1. Registration and uploading of ETP reports All eligible research scholars as per the attached list ( List of research scholars eligible for ETP) are required to register for ETP evaluation and upload their files through following UMS link: UMS Navigation -->Research & Development --> Ph.D. Scholar Activity Details --> Upcoming Activity The last date for registration and uploading of report is 30th January 2021. Step-2. Recommendation of ETP Report by the respective Supervisor/Co-supervisor/ Administrative supervisor: Once the research scholar have registered for the ETP and uploaded their ETP report for the evaluation, the same must be recommended by their respective Supervisor/Co-supervisor/Administrative supervisor by visiting the following the link: UMS navigation --> Division of Examination --> Ph.D. Evaluation Cell --> PhD Seminar File Verification --> ETP The last date for verification of the report is 2nd February 2021. Evaluation of the End Term Presentation (ETP) via online platform It is for the information of the all concerned that due to the prevailing situation, the End Term Presentation (ETP) evaluation shall be planned via online platform google meet. Important Note: For Registration and Uploading of ETP report: 1. As per current guidelines, the research scholars who are either absent or are not recommended in any Ph.D. evaluation 2 times in a row or 3 times overall, the Ph.D. admission may be deemed cancelled. Therefore, all such research scholars who have either missed or have been awarded “Not Recommended” in one or two Ph.D. evaluations are strongly advised to register for the ETP evaluation. 2. The research scholars must upload single PDF file for end term report strictly as per the attached guidelines (Guidelines for ETP February 2021) to complete the registration process or else their registration may be cancelled. 3. In case the research scholars are unable to get a signed copy of the synopsis from their respective supervisor due to prevailing situation, they can upload the soft copy of the synopsis without supervisor signature. But it is required that the synopsis uploaded by them must be strictly as per the guidelines and it must be verified by their supervisor through UMS interface as per prescribed timelines. 4. Research scholars are also required to submit 2 hard copies of the reports duly verified and signed by the respective supervisor/ co-supervisor/ administrative supervisor (wherever applicable) in Research Degree and Evaluation Cell (RDEC) (Block-30; Room Number- 302B) for which the separate communication shall be made in due course of time. 5. File containing PDF of snapshots of pages is strictly prohibited and shall not be considered for evaluation. 6. No extension shall be given for registration for ETP beyond the last date. 7. Research scholars should go through the attachment (Snapshots for using ETP registration interface) before registering and uploading the ETP reports at the interface. For Recommendation of the ETP Report: 1. The research scholar must upload the ETP report well in advance so that it can be recommended by the respective Supervisor/Co-supervisor/Administrative supervisor within the stipulated timelines. For online evaluation of the End Term Presentation (ETP) a) The research scholar must have laptop/ desktop or any other suitable mean with proper audio/ video facility. b) The research scholar must have high speed internet facility to appear for the online ETP evaluation. In case, the research scholar has registered for the ETP evaluation but could not appear for the same due to any issue, he/she shall be marked absent for the evaluation. Result of all such research scholars for ETP evaluation shall stand as “Not Recommended” and the will be required to re-register for the next scheduled ETP evaluation with subject to meeting all other eligibility criteria. c) The research scholar must be well versed with the online google meet platform. It is strongly advised that the research scholar must present his/ her presentation to the respective supervisor prior to appearing in actual ETP evaluation so that there is no confusion on the day of evaluation. In case, any of the eligible research scholars has query, write us at rdc.etrs@lpu.co.in

title: Registration for State of the Art Seminar (SAS) of Ph.D. Scholars (Ref. No. LPU/DOE/IC/210105/001) : (1/5/2021)
body: This is in reference to the evaluation of State of the Art Seminar (SAS) which will be conducted tentatively in Feb-March 2021. It is mandatory for all research scholars to clear SAS within two years from the date of registration otherwise their admission may be deemed as cancelled. The key points for SAS evaluation are as follows: a) To finalize the Title of the proposed research work. b) To finalize the Objectives of the proposed research work. c) To finalize the research methodology of the proposed research work. I. The research scholars are required to follow the following three steps to be eligible for appearing in SAS. 1. Registration for SAS: Research scholars who have successfully completed their course work or exempted from the course work (due to M.Phil.) can register for SAS seminar through the interface available in the UMS at the following link. UMS Navigation --> Research & Development --> SAS Registration form Interface for registration will remain active from 5th Jan 2021 to 25th Jan 2021. Only those research scholars should register for their SAS seminar who are willing to appear for the evaluation in the month Feb-March 2021 and have the approval of their respective Supervisor/Co-supervisor for the same. 2. Uploading of synopsis: Once the research scholar has registered for the SAS, he/ she needs to upload the synopsis for the same (within a stipulated time period) which shall be evaluated by the panel of experts. The research scholar needs to visit the same UMS link for uploading of the synopsis of SAS along with the other relevant documents. UMS Navigation --> Research & Development -->SAS Registration form The last date for uploading the synopsis report is 2nd Feb, 2021. 3. Recommendation of the synopsis by the respective Supervisor/ Co-supervisor/ Administrative supervisor: Once the research scholar has uploaded the synopsis for the evaluation, the same must be recommended by the respective Supervisor/ Co-supervisor/ Administrative supervisor by visiting the following the link: UMS link: UMS navigation --> Division of Examination --> Ph.D. --> Scholar File Verification --> SAS --> Download The last date for verification of the synopsis is 7th Feb, 2021. II. Evaluation of the State of the Art Seminar (SAS) via online platform: It is for the information of the all concerned that due to prevailing situation the SAS evaluation shall be planned via online platform google meet. Important Note: For Registration: a) At the time of SAS registration, the research scholars should opt of their domain for their SAS Seminar very carefully after consulting with their Supervisors/Co-Supervisors/Administrative Supervisor (if any) as they will be evaluated by the expert panel from the selected domain only. No request for change in domain shall be entertained afterwards. b) No extension shall be given for registration beyond the last date. c) No request for deregistration shall be entertained beyond the last date of registration and the scholar shall be marked absent. d) Research scholars having pending dues are not eligible to register for the SAS evaluation. Therefore, research scholars are requested to clear the pending dues and get registered for the SAS evaluation before the last date. e) If a research scholar registers for the SAS evaluation but is absent at the date of seminar/evaluation then he/she shall be required to re-register for the next scheduled SAS evaluation with the applicability of fee of Rs. 5000/- with subject to meeting all other eligibility criteria. He/ she shall only be allowed to appear in next scheduled SAS (scheduled tentatively from April 2021 onwards) only after the clearance of fine. For Uploading Synopsis: a) The research scholar shall not be eligible for uploading any synopsis report without completing registration process. b) The research scholars are strongly advised that synopsis file must be uploaded only after the thorough discussion with the Supervisor. Same should be defended during the presentation on the day of evaluation. For preparing the presentation the research scholar should refer to the format for SAS presentation (Attachment) c) No extension shall be given for uploading synopsis report beyond the last date. d) Read the attached guidelines very carefully before uploading the synopsis. e) All the research scholars must upload single PDF file for the synopsis including Annexure-I as per the attached guidelines or else their SAS registration may be cancelled. He/she shall be required to re-register for the next scheduled SAS evaluation (with fee of Rs. 5000/-). No second chance shall be given to upload the synopsis. f) Research scholars should go through the attachment (Snapshots for using SAS registration interface) before registering and uploading the synopsis at the interface. For recommendation of the Synopsis: a) The research scholar must upload the synopsis well in advance so that it can be recommended by the respective Supervisor/ Co-supervisor/ Administrative supervisor within the stipulated timelines. For online evaluation of the State of the Art Seminar (SAS): a) The research scholar must have laptop/ desktop or any other suitable mean with proper audio/ video facility. b) The research scholar must have high speed internet facility to appear for the online SAS evaluation. In case, the research scholar has registered for the SAS evaluation but could not appear for the same due to any issue, he/she shall be marked absent for the evaluation and he/shall be required to re-register for the next scheduled SAS evaluation with the applicability of fee of Rs. 5000/- with subject to meeting all other eligibility criteria. c) The research scholar must be well versed with the online google meet platform. It is strongly advised that the research scholar must present his/ her presentation to the respective supervisor prior to appearing in actual SAS evaluation so that there is no confusion on the day of evaluation. All the research scholars who have completed two years from date of registration and have the last chance to appear in the SAS seminar in Feb-March 2021 are advised to avail this chance as no further extension shall be given for the same. In case, any of the eligible research scholars has query regarding the following issues: 1. Registration/Uploading of synopsis write at rdc.sas@lpu.co.in or contact Ms. Poonam (7986479141)/ Dr. Jashanpreet Singh (8968875079) 2. Supervisor / Co-supervisor /fee related query write at drp@lpu.co.in

title: Enrollment into Career Services-2022 graduating batch (first year and non-first year students) - Timelines as on 01-Jan-2021 : (1/2/2021)
body: Kind attention: First year and Non-first year students expected to graduate in 2022. The university has always offered an immense support to its students in shaping their career. Keeping in mind the current employment scenario and aspirations of the students, as a very special gesture, University is extending the deadline of Career Services Registration till 28th Feb 2021 for first year and non-first year students expected to graduate in 2022 as per following timelines: Registration Timelines (as on 01-Jan-2021): a) Career Services Registration with immediate access to placement/internship opportunities from was open till 31st Aug 2020 for non-first year students and till 12th Dec 2020 for first year students. b) Career Services Registration with access to placement/internship opportunities from 01-Jan-2021 was open from 1st Sep 2020 till 12th Dec 2020 for non-first year students. c) Career Services Registration with access to placement/internship opportunities from 01-Mar-2021 was open from 13th Dec 2020 till 31st Dec 2020 for both first year and non-first year students. d) Career Services Registration with access to placement/internship opportunities from 01-May-2021 is open from 1st Jan 2021 till 28th Feb 2021 for both first year and non-first year students. Applicability: a) The policy is applicable to students (Indian and International) of full-time regular programs (including Hons. dual-degree and integrated) expected to graduate in 2022. b) The policy is not applicable to students enrolled in ODL, Part-time, M.Phil., PhD. and Certificate programs. Registration Process: The registration process is divided into two parts- PROCESS STEP-1 and PROCESS STEP-2. For the details of Step 1 and Step 2, please refer the attached file. Students are advised to carefully read the respective policy available on placement portal before enrolling for University Career Services; same is attached below for your reference.
