title: Voter ID card detail Verification by Faculty/Staff/Students (Ref. No. LPU/DOE/IC/191005/001) : (10/5/2019)
body: Under the EVP programme of Government of India, the details mentioned in the Voter Id card must be verified by each and every citizen of India who has a Voter ID Card. The individual’s details like Name, Father Name, Date of Birth, Address etc. needs to be checked and verified on the website of Election Commission of India. The link of the website is as under:- www.nvsp.in Hence, it is mandatory for all the Staff/Faculty/Students to verify their Voter ID Card details on the Government Website. For the verification of Voter ID card details, first of all, all the Faculty/Staff/Students have to register themselves on the portal (NATIONAL VOTERS’ SERVICES PORTAL) using one time OTP obtained on the mobile number. The individual can add other family members like Wife, Husband, Children, Mother, and Father etc. also for online verification of Voter ID Card. If your Voter ID Card details are not correct then the same must be corrected through the website itself. The reference number is generated only once when you submit the verification button after checking your detail. It is advisable to take the screen shot of the reference number as it is not visible in your login after refreshing the verification page. This reference number must be saved for your record. The complete step by step process of verification is given in the enclosed word file. All are requested to complete the verification. Also all the Staff/Faculty/Students are required to fill the reference number in Google form for record purpose. The Google form link is as under:- https://tinyurl.com/VoterCardVerification This process must be updated on or before 14-10-2019. In case of any queries, you can contact Mr. Anil Dhawan, Assistant Registrar, SSIV Cell on all working days between 10.00 AM to 4.00 PM in Building No.32, Room No.101 B, Cabin No. 01.

title: Department of Soft Skills III cordially invites you to attend the Workshop on “Time Management” : (10/3/2019)
body: Department of Soft Skills III cordially invites you to attend the Workshop on “Time Management” “It’s not about having time, it’s about making time” A WARM GREETING TO ALL VERTOS!! Considering the speed at which Industry changes these days, one thing is certain: if you can’t manage your time effectively, you will have a hard time managing anything else. Yet, most people waste precious minutes, hours, even days, reacting to what is going on around them rather than developing skills that will keep them moving forward and accomplishing their most important goals. Department of Soft Skills III, under the aegis of Centre for Professional Enhancement-III is organizing a workshop on “TIME MANAGEMENT” The workshop intends to help students understand the importance of time management. * Set goals and prioritize them to determine if activities are goal-directed *Achieve better results through effective planning and clarifying objectives *Gain a balance between academic goals and overall personality development goals by participating in co-curricular and extracurricular activities *Use time management tools more effectively *Manage resources more efficiently Who all can participate? Do you juggle between studies, work, social life, family, hobbies, personal interests, and commitments? Do you want to come out of this vicious circle of juggling and feeling of being lost in life? If YES, then you are welcome to this workshop on time management. It is open for all students of Lovely Professional University. title: METAL - VERBATTLE Debate Contest (9/30/2019)

title: Prevention from Dengue Fever : (9/21/2019)
body: Dengue virus is transmitted by a bite from the Aedes aegypti mosquito. Only the female mosquito transmits the dengue virus. This mosquito is a daytime biter, both inside and outside homes, and is most active in the hours after sunrise and before sunset. Aedes aegypti mosquitoes breed inside and outside the home in containers holding water and rarely fly more than 200 meters from the breeding site. They do not breed in creeks, swamps, pools or other bodies of water. --Signs and symptoms This disease has a sudden onset and symptoms may include: • Fever for 3 to 7 days • Intense headache and pain behind the eyes • Muscle and joint pain • Loss of appetite • Vomiting and diarrhea • Skin rash • Bleeding, usually from the nose or gums. Recovery is sometimes associated with prolonged fatigue and depression. Repeated episodes of dengue fever may result in excessive bleeding and shock but, with appropriate treatment, are rarely fatal. --Prevention • There is no vaccine to prevent human infection by this virus. • Wear long, loose fitting, light coloured clothing, covering as much of the body as you can. Mosquitoes can bite through tight clothing like jeans. • Personal protection and the environmental management of mosquitoes are important in preventing illness. • When outdoors, apply insect repellent containing DEET (diethyl toluamide) or picaridin and always follow instructions on the label. • Place mosquito-proof mesh on doors and windows. • Cover your sleeping areas with mosquito nets. Aerosol knockdown or surface insect sprays can help control mosquitoes inside the home but always follow instructions on the label. - All hostel student/staff to ensure that Desert Cooler installed at their rooms to be kept dry when not in use.

title: Prevention from Fungal Infection : (9/19/2019)
body: Ringworm is a fungal skin infection that causes a red, circular, itchy rash. Take care of yourself to prevent this infection. Do’s -Regular bathing, Body cleansing is must -Before wearing clothes, drying out yourself to prevent excess moisture -Wearing loose clothes -Laundering clothes of infected person in hot water and washing with anti-septic agent -Drying clothes in sunlight for at least 2 hours. -Wearing clothes after ironing them and placing them separately -Washing your hands with anti-septic and water frequently. -Keeping hair, nails and scalp clean -Wearing well ventilated shoes with cotton socks, not sharing comb and other utilities with other family members. -Eating healthy food which boost immunity, drinking 2-3 liters of water everyday

title: A team building, group interaction and confidence building workshop Hrudhya (9/14/2019)
body: Subject: A team building, group interaction and confidence building workshop Hrudhya Dear Vertos When we fear public speaking or are required to give a speech you may ask yourself why is public speaking important? Believe it or not but public speaking is one of the most important skills you will ever develop in your life. Public speaking is so important that it could be the deciding factor in many things such as your career development, your business growth and even in the relationships you have with your friends and family. Public speaking is a skill worth learning. Department of Verbal Ability under the aegis of Centre for Professional Enhancement is going to conduct a workshop Hrudhya. The students will understand the lifecycle of leadership. Its components would be explained. A small activity will be performed to define ones priorities. Small games will be played to make the session interactive. Lastly, as a person can never be a leader without a dream therefore, students will tell about their own dreams. The main objectives of the workshop will be: To define ones priority. Conduction of group games will be there to engage with audience to justify the acceptance for different perceptions. Details of the Workshop: Registration link: https://tinyurl/hrudyaworkshop Resource person: Ms. Tanvi Bhasin, Soft Skills Trainer, Lovely Professional University.. title: Bajaj Finserve EON Season II : (9/12/2019)
body: All MBA First Year and Final Year Students are advised to register for the Bajaj Finserv EON Season II before 23rd August. Bajaj Finance Limited is the most diversified and profitable non-bank in the country with a wide portfolio of products spread across Consumer, SME & Commercial Lending as well as Wealth Management. We are excited to Introduce you to EON - a unique B-school competition that gives students an opportunity to LEARN about the finance sector and to help build their career. The focus of EON is to give an opportunity to the students to understand the workings of an NBFC. The game is played in team of three students each. In this competition, participants will have to build their own NBFC with two sales and one credit officer. The teams need to grow their business by lending to the right customers and stay profitable. The game will be played over four quarters (one quarter runs for two days) and across three different product categories. The teams will have to take the right decisions of selecting & approving the right customers and earn individual incentives. The team with the most profitable NBFC at the end of the fourth quarter wins. Download the ‘Bajaj Finance EON’ app from their respective play stores by clicking on Google Play Store for Android or App Store for IOS, and get started. This is your opportunity to Explore A New Reality!Bajaj Finance EONDownload. Register and Play.

title: Prevention from Dengue Fever : (9/6/2019)
body: Dengue virus is transmitted by a bite from the Aedes aegypti mosquito. Only the female mosquito transmits the dengue virus. This mosquito is a daytime biter, both inside and outside homes, and is most active in the hours after sunrise and before sunset. Aedes aegypti mosquitoes breed inside and outside the home in containers holding water and rarely fly more than 200 meters from the breeding site. They do not breed in creeks, swamps, pools or other bodies of water. --Signs and symptoms This disease has a sudden onset and symptoms may include: • Fever for 3 to 7 days • Intense headache and pain behind the eyes • Muscle and joint pain • Loss of appetite • Vomiting and diarrhea • Skin rash • Bleeding, usually from the nose or gums. Recovery is sometimes associated with prolonged fatigue and depression. Repeated episodes of dengue fever may result in excessive bleeding and shock but, with appropriate treatment, are rarely fatal. --Prevention • There is no vaccine to prevent human infection by this virus . • Wear long, loose fitting, light coloured clothing, covering as much of the body as you can. Mosquitoes can bite through tight clothing like jeans. • Personal protection and the environmental management of mosquitoes are important in preventing illness. • When outdoors, apply insect repellent containing DEET (diethyl toluamide) or picaridin and always follow instructions on the label. • Place mosquito-proof mesh on doors and windows. • Cover your sleeping areas with mosquito nets. Aerosol knockdown or surface insect sprays can help control mosquitoes inside the home but always follow instructions on the label. - All hostel student/staff to ensure that Desert Cooler installed at their rooms to be kept dry when not in use.

title: GRE/GMAT Coaching inside LPU Campus by AptiGuide Institute. : (9/5/2019)
body: Dear Students, GRE stands for Graduate Record Examination and is for Admission inMasters Programs and GMAT stands for Graduate Management Admission Test and is for Admission in MBA Programs. GRE and GMAT are standardized assessment tests to gauge whether a student is fit for aGraduate Programs in various Graduate schools across USA, Canada, Germany, Singapore,Australia, Europe, India and a lot of other countries. In fact, Scholarships for the prestigious Graduate programs across all these nations have GRE and GMAT as a prevalent deciding factor. These Scholarships cover up to 100% of thetuition fee of a student. GRE and GMAT are valid for 5 years and can be taken throughout the year. Generally students take it in their 5 th to 7 th Semester. Classes for the preparation of GRE and GMAT Exam are going on inside the campus in Block 14 Room No. 14-110. These classes are being conducted by AptiGuide Institute, which is one the most renowned Institute of the Region. Interested students can Enquire at 9872270597 and also register on the following link fora counselling session with Experts from AptiGuide, : https://tinyurl.com/aglpuenq For attending a demo class, Please register on this link:https://tinyurl.com/aptiguidedemo1 AptiGuide’s Office address : Block 13, Room 206, Cabin - 17

body: Dear All, Department of Foreign Languages (DFL) is pleased to inform that the admissions for Certification Course in Chinese (Mandarin) Language has now begun. Courses Offered: Programme Name (Semester 1) Duration Course Code Certificate in Chinese Language - HSK Level 60 hours CHIS101 Career Options: - Interpreter: It involves the conversion of conversation in Chinese to English and vice-versa. - Translator: The profile requires the candidate to convert written documents from Chinese to English and vice-versa. - IT and Automobile Companies: Many Chinese Companies and Indian Companies prefer candidates with Technical Knowledge along with Chinese Skills as most of their clients are China. - Research Analyst: When it comes to large companies that have competition in countries like China and other Mandarin-speaking nations, having Chinese language skills are a major plus when investigating information that may not be available in English. - Work in China: After learning the advanced level of Chinese, the opportunities are open for candidates to work in China. - Outbound Process: There are several BPOs which are dealing with Chinese Clients and they look for candidates who can provide them Language support. - Teaching: There are opportunities for those who want to add value by teaching Chinese in Schools, Colleges, Institution and Corporate Offices. body: All the Ph.D. Scholars who have registered for their respective Ph.D. programs before July 2016 and have successfully completed their State of The Art (SOTA) evaluation are required to register for End Term Report (ETR). The registration and file uploading process for ETR shall be starting from 3rd September 2019 onwards. The main aim of the End Term Report (ETR) is as follows: a. To present the action taken against the suggestions given by the Department Doctoral Board (DDB) panel members in the last evaluation. b. Justification in case a particular suggestion is not incorporated c. To present amount of work done or progress made since last evaluation All eligible scholars as per the attached list (List of scholars eligible for ETR in Oct 2019) can register for ETR evaluation and upload their files through following UMS link: UMS Navigation ---->Research & Development ----> Ph.D. Scholar Activity Details ----> Upcoming Activity The last date for registration and uploading of report is 25th September 2019. Note- 1. As per current guidelines, for all the scholars who are either absent or are not recommended in any Ph.D. evaluation 2 times in a row or 3 times overall, the Ph.D. admission may be deemed cancelled. Therefore, all such scholars are strongly advised to register for the upcoming ETR. 2. All the scholars must upload single PDF file for End Term Report duly verified and signed by respective supervisors strictly as per the attached guidelines to complete the registration process or else their registration may be cancelled. 3. File containing PDF of snapshots of pages is strictly prohibited and shall not be considered for evaluation. 4. No extension shall be given for uploading report beyond the last date. 5. Students should go through the attachment (Snapshots for using ETR registration interface) before registering and uploading the End Term Reports at the interface. Any queries can be directed to Ms. Astha Malhotra through rdc.etrs@lpu.co.in or in Block-Room: 30-508A.

title: Effective Negotiation Skills Using NLP : (9/2/2019)
body: Department of Soft Skills under the aegis of Centre for Professional Enhancement is organizing a workshop on “Effective Negotiation Skills Using NLP” to enlighten the students about the Practical Negotiation Framework, Handling relationship issues in Negotiations, Tactics for Handling Difficult Negotiators, The Art of Negotiation. Highly interactive program and focuses on the practical aspects of realistic negotiation skills development through experiential learning. A variety of learning methodologies such as the Accelerated Learning Principles (ALP) and Neuro Linguistic Programming (NLP) will be used to sustain the participant’s interest and to create an optimum learning environment that will maximize the learning outcomes. Objectives: 1. Negotiating with confidence using NLP Anchoring 2. Guidelines for negotiating in different situations 3. Building good working negotiation relationships 4. Handling difficult negotiators and situations 5. Neutralizing Hardball tactics 6. Silence as a negotiation tool with NLP techniques 7. Breaking negotiation deadlocks Target Audience: The target audience for the workshop will be the students across the University. Course duration: Sunday 10.00AM – 1PM Course Fee: Rs 100/- per participant.Fee can be paid to accounts department or Paytm at 9717282201 For Registration: Visit to Shortto.com/cpeevent and select “Effective Negotiation Skills Using NLP”. body: LPU in collaboration with La Trobe University Australia gives an amazing opportunity to the students for the “Technology Infusion Grand Challenge” Entries are now open to an annual innovation competition for students called the Technology Infusion Grand Challenge. Applications are till 15th September 2019. Who is Eligible: Students in their final two years of undergraduate studies in Science, Technology, Engineering, Mathematics and/or Business Studies. This competition provides a great opportunity for students to showcase their talents and gain exposure on the global stage. What’s the fee: Taking part in the competition is free of charge What’s the Reward: The winner of the competition will be awarded a 2-week mentorship stay in Melbourne where they will be given the opportunity to work with academic and business experts at La Trobe University's Centre for Technology Infusion in Melbourne, Australia. Selected student teams could also receive an investment of up to $1000 to develop their prototype What’s the process: To participate in this competition, you need to fill an application form and provide a letter of support from your Head of Department. Your team must consist of three to five students, preferably with gender diversity. Only enter the personal details of your team leader to register. Once you have registered, the application form and a template for the letter of support will be emailed to you. Check the details https://www.latrobe.edu.au/technology-infusion/grand-challenge and reach out for guidance to Ms. Supriya Mathew, Supriya.22515@lpu.co.in,int.partnership@lpu.co.in

title: Club MRIDA cordially invites you to attend the Activity on “Picture Perception and Description.” : (8/26/2019)
body: Club MRIDA cordially invites you to attend the Activity on “Picture Perception and Description” “Life is weird and complex but very simple at the same time. It's all about PERCEPTION.”—Tyler Posey A WARM GREETING TO ALL VERTOS! There are some questions for which one wishes to seek answers: When is a surface with marks on it called a "picture”? How do pictures carry meaning? What kinds of meaning can pictures carry? Is there a grammar of picturing? Is picture perception essentially innate, or is it a skill that must be learned? Once you decide what a picture is, you will be able to understand what it conveys or how to interpret it. Perception refers to the cognition of what one sees. Enhancing picture perception skills improves one’s decision making and reasoning skills and helps in brainstorming. title: Center for Professional Enhancement III cordially invites you to attend the “Workshop on Accent Neutralization” : (8/23/2019)
body: Center for Professional Enhancement III cordially invites you to attend the “Workshop on Accent Neutralization” A WARM GREETING TO ALL VERTOS! The need for speaking in a neutral accent has been growing today because the customers and the clients have to interact in a universal language in a globally acceptable style and accent. Moreover, during an interview it is crucial to not let your accent be recruiter’s focus of attention, it may trigger an emotional response which may or may not be desirable. Department of Soft Skills II under the aegis of Center for Professional Enhancement-III is organizing a Workshop on Accent Neutralization. Accent neutralization is not about adopting a new accent, and speaking like someone a person is not. Accent neutralization helps employees to get over stronger regional twangs and accents, and speak in a more neutral fashion so that callers from anywhere in the globe can understand them clearly. Who all can participate? It is open for all students of Lovely Professional University who would like to learn the art of accent neutralization to take giants steps in their career. Timings: 05:00-06:00 p.m. Venue: 28-208 Training cost per student : Rs. 500 Registration Process: 1. An amount of Rs. 500 need to be submitted in accounts department 32-103 under fees for ""Revenue Workshop on Accent Neutralization" 2. body: This is in reference to the evaluation of Annual seminar which will be starting tentatively from September 2019 onwards. title: Prevention from Fungal Infection : (8/17/2019)
body: Ringworm is a fungal skin infection that causes a red, circular, itchy rash. Take care of yourself to prevent this infection. Do’s -Regular bathing, Body cleansing is must -Before wearing clothes, drying out yourself to prevent excess moisture -Wearing loose clothes -Laundering clothes of infected person in hot water and washing with anti-septic agent -Drying clothes in sunlight for at least 2 hours. -Wearing clothes after ironing them and placing them separately -Washing your hands with anti-septic and water frequently. -Keeping hair, nails and scalp clean -Wearing well ventilated shoes with cotton socks, not sharing comb and other utilities with other family members. -Eating healthy food which boost immunity, drinking 2-3 liters of water everyday

title: Club ELECTECH cordially invites you to attend the Workshop on “Moral Dilemma” : (8/14/2019)
body: “How can one be well...when one suffers morally?” ? Leo Tolstoy, War and Peace A WARM GREETING TO ALL VERTOS!! Are there situations where right and wrong aren't perfectly clear? Yes! These are called "moral dilemmas" and sometimes we have to "step into someone else's shoes" in order to come to an agreement. CLUB ELECTECH, under the aegis of Centre for Professional Enhancement-III is organizing a workshop on “Moral Dilemma” This workshop will help the students to consider a moral dilemma and make initial judgements on the situation independently. Students will be engaged in discussion weighing different perspectives in different situations involving a Moral Dilemma. They will be introduced to the terms "morals," "moral dilemma" and "perspectives." Questions will be specific and discussion will be largely guided. Who all can participate? It is open for all students of Lovely Professional University who would like to evaluate a moral dilemma both on their own and as a group. body: This is for the information of all the concerned that remedial classes have been planned for the students who will register in the upcoming re-appear examination (Autumn Term-19201). The courses being offered in these classes are mentioned in the attachment. The classes for a course shall span 10 lectures each of one hour duration, out of which 5 lectures shall be held in time slots 8.00 -9:00 am or 5:00 -6.00 pm and rest 5 lectures shall be held between 9:00am to 5:00pm. title: Prevention from Dengue Fever : (8/9/2019)
body: Dengue virus is transmitted by a bite from the Aedes aegypti mosquito. Only the female mosquito transmits the dengue virus. This mosquito is a daytime biter, both inside and outside homes, and is most active in the hours after sunrise and before sunset. Aedes aegypti mosquitoes breed inside and outside the home in containers holding water and rarely fly more than 200 meters from the breeding site. They do not breed in creeks, swamps, pools or other bodies of water. --Signs and symptoms This disease has a sudden onset and symptoms may include: • Fever for 3 to 7 days • Intense headache and pain behind the eyes • Muscle and joint pain • Loss of appetite • Vomiting and diarrhea • Skin rash • Bleeding, usually from the nose or gums. Recovery is sometimes associated with prolonged fatigue and depression. Repeated episodes of dengue fever may result in excessive bleeding and shock but, with appropriate treatment, are rarely fatal. --Prevention • There is no vaccine to prevent human infection by this virus. • Wear long, loose fitting, light coloured clothing, covering as much of the body as you can. Mosquitoes can bite through tight clothing like jeans. • Personal protection and the environmental management of mosquitoes are important in preventing illness. • When outdoors, apply insect repellent containing DEET (diethyl toluamide) or picaridin and always follow instructions on the label. • Place mosquito-proof mesh on doors and windows. • Cover your sleeping areas with mosquito nets. Aerosol knockdown or surface insect sprays can help control mosquitoes inside the home but always follow instructions on the label. - All hostel student/staff to ensure that Desert Cooler installed at their rooms to be kept dry when not in use.

title: Blood Donation Camp on 09th August, 2019 organize by “Samarpan …a lifeline & LPUNSS” : (8/7/2019)
body: Do you feel you don’t have much to offer? You have the most precious resource of all: the ability to save a life by donating blood! Help share this invaluable gift with someone in need. Rarely do we get a chance to serve the society especially if it is a matter of saving some one’s life. Luckily on 09th August, 2019 each one of us is getting a chance to save three lives. A Voluntary blood donation camp is being organized by “LPUNSS” & “Samarpan …a lifeline” an initiative of Community Service Cell, Division of Student Affairs in association with Civil Hospital, Jalandhar. Do you know that, o Every 3 out of 10 people in India need blood? o 75% of the voluntary donors in our country donate only once per year? o This shortage can be overcome if just 2% of our country's youth donate blood? Date: 09th August, 2019 Time: 09:30 AM – 5:00 PM Venue: Block 28 (Basement) Note: Duty Leaves for Donors 2 Hour of Duration For more details Visit facebook.com/lpunss or Instagram.com/lpu_nss

title: Registration for R grade viva of Projects, Dissertation or similar courses. (Ref. No. LPU/DOE/IC/190807/003) : (8/7/2019)
body: All the students awarded with R grade (in term Spring Term 18192, Summer Term 1819W) in Capstone Projects, Dissertations, and similar courses (List attached) are required to register for R grade for which the final ETP evaluation shall be scheduled from last week of Aug 2019 onwards. The students are required to ensure the following points for R grade Registration. 1. Filling of Online Registration Form: Students are required to fill the online R grade registration form and to pay R grade registration fee online via visiting following UMS Link: (for detailed process refer attachment 1) UMS Navigation------>Reappear Registration--------> Registration Form The Last date for R grade registration and fee payment is 14th August. 2019 (without any late fee) and 21st August.2019 (with late fee of Rs.2000/-) No request of R grade registration shall be entertained after 21st August.2019. 2. Uploading Soft Copy of Report: Students are required to upload the soft copy of final report (if required) for the courses as per the information available in attachment3 (i.e. List of Projects, Dissertation and similar courses) via visiting the following UMS link UMS Navigation------>LMS--------> Upload Research Project It is mandatory for the students to get the online recommendation on the same by respective Supervisor. The last date to upload soft copy of report and getting online recommendation of supervisor is 22nd Aug 2019. 3. Final Report Submission in A.O office Students are required to take the print out of fee receipt generated online along with the final hard copy report duly signed by the supervisor and visit the respective AO office for getting the final hard copy report signed and stamped by the AO officer. The final hard copy report signed and stamped by the AO need to be produced on the day of R grade viva by the student. Important Note: 1) AO officer will take the submission through online mode till 5PM on 22nd Aug 2019. 2) R Grade viva schedule shall be communicated to the students via UMS my messages at least 7 days in advance from the ETP viva date. 3) In case a student does not register for R grade or misses the report submission as per UMS timelines then R grade viva shall not be conducted and grade would be converted to F. Any queries can be directed to Mr. Mohit Prakram, (COC), Projects and Internships Cell on academic.evaluation@lpu.co.in or in Block-Room: 29-401.

title: Club ELECTECH cordially invites you to attend the Workshop on Waqt Ki Kimat (8/5/2019)
body: A WARM GREETING TO ALL VERTOS! Time management is the process of planning and controlling how much time to spend on specific activities. Good time management enables an individual to complete more in a shorter period of time, lowers stress, and leads to career success. CLUB ELECTECH, under the aegis of Center for Professional Enhancement-III is organizing a Workshop on Waqt Ki Kimat. Good time management allows you to accomplish more in a shorter period of time, which leads to more free time, which lets you take advantage of learning opportunities, lowers your stress, and helps you focus, which leads to more career success. Each benefit of time management improves another aspect of your life. There are so many reasons why time management is important at work. It is one of the most sought after qualities for employees to have, and with good reason. Managers need to be able to assess their workers productivity and make sure they are getting the most out of their employees. Not only is it good for business, but it is also a skill that can be of benefit to the workers themselves. Who all can participate? It is open for all students of Lovely Professional University who would like to enhance their time management skills. title: CoCubes (Pre assess -1) Exam for (Engineering/MCA) placement registered students graduating in 2020. (8/4/2019)
body: Dear Aspirants, Centre for Professional Enhancement has scheduled a renowned exam named CoCubes (Pre Assess-1) for 2020 batch placement registered students(Engineering/MCA) on 08thAug , 2019. Good Score in CoCubes will give you many benefits like better career opportunities, better Training sessions etc. So come prepared and attempt the exam with full enthusiasm. Why CoCubes Exam is important: CoCubes is an industry renowned testing platform. Most of the companies use CoCubes as their testing platform during placement drives. CoCubes is India’s largest assessment and hiring platform. CoCubes helps us in gauging your current performance levels which will be utilized to design customized training inputs for the students. You can attempt any module at any time within the given time span (9 AM, to 11 PM). Score of this exam will also be considered for shortlisting students for special training and companies therefore students should attempt this seriously. Action will be taken as per PEP policy against those who will not take this exam, hence attempt the test with full spirit. No Duty Leave will be provided for test attempts. Exam will be in auto-proctored mode. Therefore, don’t use any unfair means during exam. Kindly read the instructions/guidelines carefully before taking the exam. body: Dear Vertos, A Mentor is an experienced adviser and counselor who shall assist the students who are slow learners to enhance their academic performance and identify the learning difficulties faced by these students and provide them with the remedial solutions. title: Registration for Re-appear/Improvement examination to be conducted in August- November, 2019 (Ref. No. LPU/DOE/IC/190801/003) : (8/1/2019)
body: The interface for registration of Re-appear/Improvement examination to be conducted in August- November, 2019 has been opened for all students. A student having ‘E’ grade(s) in any course code(s) (of any term) will be automatically registered in all his/her ‘E’ grade courses from the backend. In case, a student does not want to appear in some of the registered courses then he/she can de-register the course(s) through the provided interface. For the final selected courses, the student is required to directly pay the fee for the ‘E’ grade courses, thus omitting the first step of registration process. In case, a course is de-registered by mistake then the same can be registered again by the student through the online interface. However, for improvement exam, the student will have to select the course code for which he/she wants to appear for the improvement. The detailed procedure is attached for reference. The tentative dates of examination for each course code have also been mentioned against the course code, so that the students can select their courses and prepare for them accordingly. The fee for re-appear registration is Rs. 350/- per course code and the last date with this fee is 16th August, 2019. Note that after 16th August, 2019 (12.00 a.m. onwards), the fee for registration will be increased to Rs. 500/- per course code and the last date with this fee is 19th August, 2019. Note: The student who fails to pay fee by 19th August, 2019 will be automatically de-registered in the pending ‘E’ grade courses for which they have not paid the fee and these courses shall stop reflecting in their account. For any scheduled lectures falling in the time slot of the examination, duty leave shall be given to the student for those lectures only (particularly in the time slot of exam time). In addition, duty leave shall also be given to the student for classes scheduled one hour prior and one hour after the time of examination. Important dates:- Registration start date 01st Aug, 2019 Last date of registration (without late fee) 16th Aug, 2019 Last date of registration (with late fee) 19th Aug, 2019 Display of seating plan-cum-final date sheet on UMS 20th Aug, 2019 Exam Start from 24th Aug, 2019

title: Prevention from Dengue Fever : (7/29/2019)
body: Dengue virus is transmitted by a bite from the Aedes aegypti mosquito. Only the female mosquito transmits the dengue virus. This mosquito is a daytime biter, both inside and outside homes, and is most active in the hours after sunrise and before sunset. Aedes aegypti mosquitoes breed inside and outside the home in containers holding water and rarely fly more than 200 meters from the breeding site. They do not breed in creeks, swamps, pools or other bodies of water. --Signs and symptoms This disease has a sudden onset and symptoms may include: • Fever for 3 to 7 days • Intense headache and pain behind the eyes • Muscle and joint pain • Loss of appetite • Vomiting and diarrhea • Skin rash • Bleeding, usually from the nose or gums. Recovery is sometimes associated with prolonged fatigue and depression. Repeated episodes of dengue fever may result in excessive bleeding and shock but, with appropriate treatment, are rarely fatal. --Prevention • There is no vaccine to prevent human infection by this virus. • Wear long, loose fitting, light coloured clothing, covering as much of the body as you can. Mosquitoes can bite through tight clothing like jeans. • Personal protection and the environmental management of mosquitoes are important in preventing illness. • When outdoors, apply insect repellent containing DEET (diethyl toluamide) or picaridin and always follow instructions on the label. • Place mosquito-proof mesh on doors and windows. • Cover your sleeping areas with mosquito nets. Aerosol knockdown or surface insect sprays can help control mosquitoes inside the home but always follow instructions on the label. - All hostel student/staff to ensure that Desert Cooler installed at their rooms to be kept dry when not in use.

title: Registration for State of the Art Seminar (SOTA) of Ph.D. Scholars. (Ref. No. LPU/DOE/IC/190726/001) : (7/26/2019)
body: This is in reference to the evaluation of State of the Art Seminar (SOTA) seminar which will be starting tentatively from 18th Sept. 2019 onwards. It is mandatory for all research scholars to clear SOTA seminar within two years from the date of registration otherwise their admission may be deemed as cancelled. The main aim of the SOTA seminar is as follows: a) To finalize the Title of the proposed research work. b) To finalize the Objectives of the proposed research work. c) To finalize the research methodology of the proposed research work. The scholars are required to follow the following 2 steps to be eligible for appearing in SOTA. 1. Registration for SOTA Scholars who have successfully completed their course work or exempted from the course work (due to M.Phil.) can register for SOTA seminar through the interface available in the UMS at the following link. UMS Navigation --> Research & Development -->SOTA Registration form Interface for registration will remain active from 26th July to 9th August, 2019. Only those students should register for their SOTA seminar who are willing to appear for the seminar in the month of September 2019 and have the approval of their respective Supervisor/Co-supervisor for the same. 2. Uploading of synopsis Once the scholar has registered for the SOTA, he/ she needs to upload the synopsis for the same (within a stipulated time period) which shall be evaluated by the panel of experts. The scholar needs to visit the same UMS link for uploading of the synopsis of SOTA along with the other relevant documents. UMS Navigation --> Research & Development -->SOTA Registration form The last date for uploading the synopsis report is 26th August 2019. Important Note: For Registration: a) At the time of SOTA registration, the scholars should opt for the domain for their SOTA Seminar very carefully after consulting with their Supervisors/Co-Supervisors (if any) as they will be evaluated by the expert panel from the selected domain only. No request for change in domain shall be entertained afterwards. b) No extension shall be given for registration beyond the last date. c) Scholars having pending dues are not eligible to register for the SOTA evaluation. Therefore, scholars are requested to clear the pending dues and get registered for the SOTA evaluation before the last date. d) If a scholar registers for the SOTA evaluation but is absent at the date of seminar/ evaluation then strict action shall be taken against the scholar and fine shall also be applicable. He/ she shall only be allowed to appear in next scheduled SOTA (scheduled tentatively from Dec 2019 onwards) only after the clearance of fine. For Uploading Synopsis report: a) A scholar shall not be eligible for uploading any synopsis report without completing registration process. b) No extension shall be given for uploading synopsis report beyond the last date. c) Read the attached guidelines very carefully before uploading the synopsis. d) The synopsis report should be strictly as per the prescribed format. e) The uploaded documents must be properly verified and signed by the respective supervisor. In case, the synopsis report is not as per the format or is not signed by the supervisor, it shall be rejected and the scholar shall be considered as absent in the seminar. All penalties applicable for absentees shall be applicable to him/her. No second chance shall be given to upload the synopsis All the scholars who have completed two years from date of registration and have the last chance to appear in the SOTA seminar in September, 2019 are advised to avail this chance as no further extension shall be given for the same. In case, any of the eligible candidate has query regarding supervisor and co-supervisor can report at Block- 38 Room-202 or send a mail to drp@lpu.co.in.

title: Personality assessment for 2019 Admission Batch (7/25/2019)
body: Traits such as personality, intelligence, attitude, and beliefs are important characteristics to measure and assess. Whether you are hiring people, helping team members understand themselves and their relationships with others, or trying to figure out what you want to do with your life, its useful to assess these types of "hidden," less obvious attributes. One way to gather this information is through psychometric tests Centre for Professional Enhancement is going to conduct Personality Assessment for 2019 Admission batch to measure their Personality type. Why Personality test? · Objective and impersonal, allowing candidates to be compared in ability terms without bias. · It provides information on type of environment the candidate prefers to work within. · It gives an insight into the candidate’s preference for behaviours and opportunity to focus on areas of improvement. What Do Personality Test Measure? · Interest tests measure how people differ in their motivation, values, and opinions in relation to their interests. · Personality tests measure how people differ in their style or manner of doing things, and in the way they interact with their environment and other people. · Designed to measure candidates suitability for a role based on the required personality characteristics and cognitive skills Pathway to appear for Assessment:Login into your UMS >> UMS Navigation >> LMS >> Personality Assessment Test Head Centre For Professional Enhancement

title: Prevention from Fungal Infection : (7/20/2019)
body: Ringworm is a fungal skin infection that causes a red, circular, itchy rash. Take care of yourself to prevent this infection. Do’s -Regular bathing, Body cleansing is must -Before wearing clothes, drying out yourself to prevent excess moisture -Wearing loose clothes -Laundering clothes of infected person in hot water and washing with anti-septic agent -Drying clothes in sunlight for at least 2 hours. -Wearing clothes after ironing them and placing them separately -Washing your hands with anti-septic and water frequently. -Keeping hair, nails and scalp clean -Wearing well ventilated shoes with cotton socks, not sharing comb and other utilities with other family members. -Eating healthy food which boost immunity, drinking 2-3 liters of water everyday

title: Prevention from Dengue Fever : (7/18/2019)
body: Dengue virus is transmitted by a bite from the Aedes aegypti mosquito. Only the female mosquito transmits the dengue virus. This mosquito is a daytime biter, both inside and outside homes, and is most active in the hours after sunrise and before sunset. Aedes aegypti mosquitoes breed inside and outside the home in containers holding water and rarely fly more than 200 meters from the breeding site. They do not breed in creeks, swamps, pools or other bodies of water. --Signs and symptoms This disease has a sudden onset and symptoms may include: • Fever for 3 to 7 days • Intense headache and pain behind the eyes • Muscle and joint pain • Loss of appetite • Vomiting and diarrhea • Skin rash • Bleeding, usually from the nose or gums. Recovery is sometimes associated with prolonged fatigue and depression. Repeated episodes of dengue fever may result in excessive bleeding and shock but, with appropriate treatment, are rarely fatal. --Prevention • There is no vaccine to prevent human infection by this virus. • Wear long, loose fitting, light coloured clothing, covering as much of the body as you can. Mosquitoes can bite through tight clothing like jeans. • Personal protection and the environmental management of mosquitoes are important in preventing illness. • When outdoors, apply insect repellent containing DEET (diethyl toluamide) or picaridin and always follow instructions on the label. • Place mosquito-proof mesh on doors and windows. • Cover your sleeping areas with mosquito nets. Aerosol knockdown or surface insect sprays can help control mosquitoes inside the home but always follow instructions on the label. - All hostel student/staff to ensure that Desert Cooler installed at their rooms to be kept dry when not in use.

title: Prevention from Fungal Infection : (7/9/2019)
body: Ringworm is a fungal skin infection that causes a red, circular, itchy rash. Take care of yourself to prevent this infection. Do’s -Regular bathing, Body cleansing is must. -Before wearing clothes, drying out yourself to prevent excess moisture -Wearing loose clothes. -Laundering clothes of infected person in hot water and washing with anti-septic agent. -Drying clothes in sunlight for at least 2 hours. -Wearing clothes after ironing them and placing them separately. -Washing your hands with anti-septic and water frequently. -Keeping hair, nails and scalp clean. -Wearing well ventilated shoes with cotton socks, not sharing comb and other utilities with other family members. -Eating healthy food which boost immunity, drinking 2-3 liters of water everyday

title: Process Clarity for Summer Certification for CSE/IT/MCA students registered for placements and passing out in 2020 : (7/8/2019)
body: Dear Student, Summer Certification window was kept from 1st July 2019 to 20th July 2019 keeping in check that you will be ready for basic gatekeeper rounds of ELQ and programming after summer PEP inputs in June’19. We agreed to dates with AMCAT and Cocubes considering the fact that they are after your summer PEP inputs and expecting that you all would have practiced through the various test on MyPerfectice and Placement Season. As most of you had taken online programs for the summer certification window, you are supposed to only spend 3 hrs. in the class for either self-study or collaborative study. The involvement was kept to bare minimum to provide you maximum time for yourself. The attendance from 6th June 2019 to 20th July 2019 will be considered for the 80% attendance criteria of summer PEP attendance based on which you will not be eligible for any company whose package is above 4 lakhs /annum. Moreover, the attendance for summer PEP will also be accumulated with the next semester(Aug’19 - Dec’19) attendance as well. This is the time when you can focus on your skills and horne your basics for the upcoming drives. Now, in July’19 there will be a lot of drives popping up at very short notice between 18th July,2019 to 30th July,2019; so, be ready for the long nights and the extra efforts that you have to put in. Process to be followed for attendance during Summer Certification:- A) Classes will be held from 10 AM to 1 PM for almost all the students except for the students who are having offline training or inputs being provided by the vendor on campus such as Upgrad etc. B) Attendance will be taken at 10:00 AM everyday your respective rooms according to your timetable. For offline trainings attendance shall be taken by trainers as per their schedule. C) Multiple random attendance shall be taken in between 10:30 Am to 1:00 PM, during each random attendance the faculty will be in the class for 15 min, and if a student is not present in the class he / she shall be marked absent for the entire 3 hrs. and any student who was late (not present during the 10 AM attendance) shall be given attendance according to the time of random attendance taken for either 2 hrs. or 1 hr. depending when the student was present. D) No queries for the late reporting students will be considered for the 1st hour attendance. You can find some FAQs at: https://www.shortto.com/faqcert

title: Prevention from Dengue Fever : (7/5/2019)
body: Dengue virus is transmitted by a bite from the Aedes aegypti mosquito. Only the female mosquito transmits the dengue virus. This mosquito is a daytime biter, both inside and outside homes, and is most active in the hours after sunrise and before sunset. Aedes aegypti mosquitoes breed inside and outside the home in containers holding water and rarely fly more than 200 meters from the breeding site. They do not breed in creeks, swamps, pools or other bodies of water. --Signs and symptoms This disease has a sudden onset and symptoms may include: • Fever for 3 to 7 days • Intense headache and pain behind the eyes • Muscle and joint pain • Loss of appetite • Vomiting and diarrhea • Skin rash • Bleeding, usually from the nose or gums. Recovery is sometimes associated with prolonged fatigue and depression. Repeated episodes of dengue fever may result in excessive bleeding and shock but, with appropriate treatment, are rarely fatal. --Prevention • There is no vaccine to prevent human infection by this virus. • Wear long, loose fitting, light coloured clothing, covering as much of the body as you can. Mosquitoes can bite through tight clothing like jeans. • Personal protection and the environmental management of mosquitoes are important in preventing illness. • When outdoors, apply insect repellent containing DEET (diethyl toluamide) or picaridin and always follow instructions on the label. • Place mosquito-proof mesh on doors and windows. • Cover your sleeping areas with mosquito nets. Aerosol knockdown or surface insect sprays can help control mosquitoes inside the home but always follow instructions on the label. - All hostel student/staff to ensure that Desert Cooler installed at their rooms to be kept dry when not in use.

title: Regarding the submission of compulsory Information by the students, who opt to stay outside university premises (7/1/2019)
body: In pursuance of UGC Regulations on curbing the menace of ragging in higher educational institutions, 2009, it is mandatory for a student seeking to reside outside the university, to submit details regarding his/her accommodation to the university. Moreover, for security and safety concerns, the local authorities, including police administration, also seek accommodation related information of the students from the university from time to time. In this regard, every student who is not opting for residential facility inside the university campus is required to submit his/her accommodation details at Ums Navigation ->Important Links - >Compulsory Accommodation Details link on immediate basis. Important Note: As the information is to be shared with local authorities on demand, the information need to be compulsorily submitted before the start of classes for next session, failing which the student will not be allowed to attend classes till submission of the required documents. In case of any queries/concerns, please write at accommodation.manage@lpu.co.in or you may call at 98759-31250, between 9am to 5pm. Uploaded By: Office of HOD Accommodation Management Team

title: A confidence building event Cross Fire by The Project Voice Club (7/1/2019)
body: Dear Vertos Confidence has become a buzzword that we hear all the time. People tell us, Be confident. We read articles entitled, How to Build More Confidence. We even attend seminars and hire coaches to help us learn how to make ourselves look and feel confident. All of these things are useful, and it is a popular topic. However, have you ever thought about why confidence is so talked about? Sure, it makes us feel good to feel confident, but there is more to it than that. Confidence is actually an integral part of a health and well-being. The Project Voice Club, Verbal Ability, will organize an event Cross Fire on 27 June 2019 from 12 pm to 1:30 pm in Mittal School of Business under the aegis of LPU - Centre for Professional Enhancement for the students of summer classes to build up their confidence and enhance their speaking skills. This event will allow students to show their talent and learn new things from each other from a discussion on different topics. The main objectives of the event will be: To overcome the language barrier amongst students. To develop and enhance communication skills. Here are the details: Resource person: Ms Priya, Assistant Professor, Department of Verbal Ability, Lovely Professional University. Registration link: https://tinyurl.com/crossfireevent Date: 2nd July 2019 Venue: 14-210 Time- 12pm- 1:30pm Head Centre for Professional Enhancement

title: Prevention from Fungal Infection : (6/22/2019)
body: Ringworm is a fungal skin infection that causes a red, circular, itchy rash. Take care of yourself to prevent this infection. Do’s -Regular bathing, Body cleansing is must -Before wearing clothes, drying out yourself to prevent excess moisture -Wearing loose clothes -Laundering clothes of infected person in hot water and washing with anti-septic agent -Drying clothes in sunlight for at least 2 hours. -Wearing clothes after ironing them and placing them separately -Washing your hands with anti-septic and water frequently. -Keeping hair, nails and scalp clean -Wearing well ventilated shoes with cotton socks, not sharing comb and other utilities with other family members. -Eating healthy food which boost immunity, drinking 2-3 liters of water everyday

title: Prevention from Dengue Fever : (6/20/2019)
body: Dengue virus is transmitted by a bite from the Aedes aegypti mosquito. Only the female mosquito transmits the dengue virus. This mosquito is a daytime biter, both inside and outside homes, and is most active in the hours after sunrise and before sunset. Aedes aegypti mosquitoes breed inside and outside the home in containers holding water and rarely fly more than 200 meters from the breeding site. They do not breed in creeks, swamps, pools or other bodies of water. --Signs and symptoms This disease has a sudden onset and symptoms may include: • Fever for 3 to 7 days • Intense headache and pain behind the eyes • Muscle and joint pain • Loss of appetite • Vomiting and diarrhea • Skin rash • Bleeding, usually from the nose or gums. Recovery is sometimes associated with prolonged fatigue and depression. Repeated episodes of dengue fever may result in excessive bleeding and shock but, with appropriate treatment, are rarely fatal. --Prevention • There is no vaccine to prevent human infection by this virus. • Wear long, loose fitting, light coloured clothing, covering as much of the body as you can. Mosquitoes can bite through tight clothing like jeans. • Personal protection and the environmental management of mosquitoes are important in preventing illness. • When outdoors, apply insect repellent containing DEET (diethyl toluamide) or picaridin and always follow instructions on the label. • Place mosquito-proof mesh on doors and windows. • Cover your sleeping areas with mosquito nets. Aerosol knockdown or surface insect sprays can help control mosquitoes inside the home but always follow instructions on the label. - All hostel student/staff to ensure that Desert Cooler installed at their rooms to be kept dry when not in use.

title: PREVENTION OF SKIN FUNGAL INFECTION : (6/14/2019)
body: Ringworm is a fungal skin infection that causes a red, circular, itchy rash. Take care of yourself to prevent this infection. Do’s -Regular bathing, Body cleansing is must -Before wearing clothes, drying out yourself to prevent excess moisture -Wearing loose clothes -Laundering clothes of infected person in hot water and washing with anti-septic agent -Drying clothes in sunlight for at least 2 hours,. -Wearing clothes after ironing them and placing them separately -Washing your hands with anti-septic and water frequently. -Keeping hair, nails and scalp clean -Wearing well ventilated shoes with cotton socks, not sharing comb and other utilities with other family members. -Eating healthy food which boost immunity, drinking 2-3 liters of water everyday

title: Donation of Books and Other Literary Resources to Central Library : (6/12/2019)
body: University’s Central Library is acknowledged as ‘Knowledge Hub’ offering variety of academic resources to the students, faculty and staff. This is highly visited place in the University by users to pursue knowledge. Central Library keeps adding new resources to its collection to cater information needs of its clients. The Central Library welcomes gifts/donations of books and other literary heritage materials that extend and supplement existing collection. Your generous gifts and donations will certainly facilitate the existing and upcoming student community and will also improve the quality and quantity of resources in the Central Library. Preferred Literary Items for Gifts and Donations • Scholarly monograph • Manuscripts • Text Books • Fictions • Biographies • Dictionaries • Encyclopedias • Atlases • Journals (Single or bound volumes) • Old Book Collections • Audio-visual material • Ph.D. Thesis (Personal) in hard or Soft Copies Conditions of Acceptance of Gifts/Donations 1. Items in poor condition will generally be not accepted for the collection. 2. The Central Library reserves the right to decline an offer of material that is already available in the collection or that does not meet collection needs. 3. Library Donation Form is available in Central Library and the prospective donors need to fill and submit the same at the time of donating the items. 4. If the donation size is big and difficult to carry, University can arrange for pick-up and transportation of items to the Central Library. 5. Gifts and donations are accepted with a common understanding that all materials will become the permanent property of Central Library of Lovely Professional University. Note: Top 10 Donors name will be displayed in Central Library notice board. Donors wishing to donate rare or unique literary material are encouraged to contact the Librarian, Ph: 01824-444563 or mail at central.library@lpu.co.in.

title: Update Regarding Daily tests of 2019 PEP Classes : (6/10/2019)
body: Dear Students, As communicated before, all the students attending the summer PEP classes must take at least 3 tests from the below mentioned packages of My Perfectice on daily basis. 1. PEP-Training package- All the tests visible in this package must be attempted by the end of the day. There is no exemption. 2. PlaceMe CSE package- 1 test from this package must be attempted on daily basis. There is no exemption. 3. Programming package [Novice To Ninja (N2N) C/C++, JAVA, Python]:1 test from this package must be attempted based on technical input. For example: Student attending Java classes will take the test from Java package. Student attending Python classes will take the test from Python package. Students having inputs on Soft skills and verbal will take the test based on their choice of programming language. Students attending JS input classes will take the test on Examly on daily basis. DP students will take their test as instructed by their trainers. title: Prevention from Dengue Fever : (6/10/2019)
body: Dengue virus is transmitted by a bite from the Aedes aegypti mosquito. Only the female mosquito transmits the dengue virus. This mosquito is a daytime biter, both inside and outside homes, and is most active in the hours after sunrise and before sunset. Aedes aegypti mosquitoes breed inside and outside the home in containers holding water and rarely fly more than 200 meters from the breeding site. They do not breed in creeks, swamps, pools or other bodies of water. --Signs and symptoms This disease has a sudden onset and symptoms may include: • Fever for 3 to 7 days • Intense headache and pain behind the eyes • Muscle and joint pain • Loss of appetite • Vomiting and diarrhea • Skin rash • Bleeding, usually from the nose or gums. Recovery is sometimes associated with prolonged fatigue and depression. Repeated episodes of dengue fever may result in excessive bleeding and shock but, with appropriate treatment, are rarely fatal. --Prevention • There is no vaccine to prevent human infection by this virus. • Wear long, loose fitting, light coloured clothing, covering as much of the body as you can. Mosquitoes can bite through tight clothing like jeans. • Personal protection and the environmental management of mosquitoes are important in preventing illness. • When outdoors, apply insect repellent containing DEET (diethyl toluamide) or picaridin and always follow instructions on the label. • Place mosquito-proof mesh on doors and windows. • Cover your sleeping areas with mosquito nets. Aerosol knockdown or surface insect sprays can help control mosquitoes inside the home but always follow instructions on the label. *All hostel student/staff to ensure that Desert Cooler installed at their rooms to be kept dry when not in use.

title: Prevention from Dengue Fever : (5/29/2019)
body: Dengue virus is transmitted by a bite from the Aedes aegypti mosquito. Only the female mosquito transmits the dengue virus. This mosquito is a daytime biter, both inside and outside homes, and is most active in the hours after sunrise and before sunset. Aedes aegypti mosquitoes breed inside and outside the home in containers holding water and rarely fly more than 200 meters from the breeding site. They do not breed in creeks, swamps, pools or other bodies of water. --Signs and symptoms This disease has a sudden onset and symptoms may include: • Fever for 3 to 7 days • Intense headache and pain behind the eyes • Muscle and joint pain • Loss of appetite • Vomiting and diarrhea • Skin rash • Bleeding, usually from the nose or gums. Recovery is sometimes associated with prolonged fatigue and depression. Repeated episodes of dengue fever may result in excessive bleeding and shock but, with appropriate treatment, are rarely fatal. --Prevention • There is no vaccine to prevent human infection by this virus. • Wear long, loose fitting, light coloured clothing, covering as much of the body as you can. Mosquitoes can bite through tight clothing like jeans. • Personal protection and the environmental management of mosquitoes are important in preventing illness. • When outdoors, apply insect repellent containing DEET (diethyl toluamide) or picaridin and always follow instructions on the label. • Place mosquito-proof mesh on doors and windows. • Cover your sleeping areas with mosquito nets. Aerosol knockdown or surface insect sprays can help control mosquitoes inside the home but always follow instructions on the label. - All hostel student/staff to ensure that Desert Cooler installed at their rooms to be kept dry when not in use.

title: Updated PEP(Placement Enhancement Program) Policy For All Students of 2020 Passing-out Batch : (5/23/2019)
body: Placement Enhancement Program for all students of 2020 passing-out batch who have opted for Placements in Companies 1. 3rd Party Tests: a. Students will undergo number of 3rd party tests, some popular ones being AMCAT, Co-cubes, E-litmus & a few others b. It is mandatory for all placement registered students to participate in all the 3rd party tests. They will be treated as placement drives and all repercussions and penalty of missing a Placement Drive will be imposed on the student, incase the test is missed. c. The fine imposed will be of Rs 500/- instead of Rs 1000/- for test missed , if there is a possibility of retest to be conducted, the retest would be conducted and if the student fails to attend the same, the fine would be increased to Rs 1,000/- d. Student should be considered absent if he/she fails to acquire at least 10% marks in the basic ELQ test, such restriction will not be imposed in case of high end coding or domain specific tests. 2. Attendance of Non-credited PEP classes: a. Attendance of each Input/ test/mock drive or any other Placement preparation related activity will be counted and accumulated towards the overall academic attendance.Students have to maintain 80% attendance in all semesters and Summer PEP as well. b. University rules of detention will apply. c. If a student does not attend a mandatory session for a particular drive , student may not be permitted to participate in that particular or a certain number of drives. d. Students who do not have a minimum of 80% attendance in Summer PEP classes and at least 40% marks in all test conducted in summer PEP will only be allowed to appear for companies offering stipend upto 12000 per month or package upto 4 Lakh per year till October 31st ‘2020 e. Attendance of Summer PEP will be accumulated with the attendance of courses in next semester starting Aug’19 3. PEP Deregistration Processing Timelines: a. A 7 day request and 7 day process model. Shall be followed for the same: b. Any student who wishes to deregister from PEP needs to submit a duly filled PEP deregistration form hard copy in person in the School Placement Office and needs to collect an acknowledgement number for the same for his reference and needs to keep the same till the processing of his/ her request. (Form is available to students in the annexures of Career service policy). No soft copy of the form shall be accepted. c. Student shall continue attending PEP activities until the request for Exiting Career Services is duly approved. Attendance shall be counted till the day of approval of Placement De-registration. d. Refund/Reimbursement/Adjustment/Waiver of PEP Fee: Upon debarment or exiting from career services at any stage of time, the student will not be entitled for any refund / reimbursement / adjustment / waiver of PEP Fee already due/paid in his fee account. e. No PEP Deregistration request shall be accepted during 25th May to 31st July.

title: Allotment of Residential Facilities During Summer for Hostel Booking for Short Duration : (5/20/2019)
body: This is for the information of all the students who seek residential facilities for PEP/ Placement Drives/ Scrutiny/ Backlog/ Viva/ Skill Development Classes/ Sports or Cultural Workshop/ Summer Term/ Dissertation Work/ Freshmen Induction/ Part Time Jobs/ Training, may avail the same as per the guidelines as given below : 1. The whole process of allotment will be carried through University Management System and student has to use his/ her login ID and Password, to book the seats. 2. Category-wise Information : (a) For PEP Students : PEP students are only allowed to book hostel seat as per their schedule dates. Eligible students will follow the given procedure : (i) Hostlers for whom PEP class is starting before 31st of May : Such students can retain their present hostel seat. Online interface for booking will start from 21st May'2019 at 02:00 PM. Students can book seat through given UMS link : UMS-> Residential and Vendor Services → Residential booking → PEP Hostel Booking. (ii) Hostlers for whom PEP class is starting on after 01st June : Such students will have to get their hostel no-dues done before 31st May'19. Online interface for booking will start from 27th May'2019 at 02:00 PM. Students can book their seat through the following link in Summer Hostel and stay will be given from 01st Jun.'2019 : UMS-> Residential and Vendor Services → Residential booking → Hostel Booking for Short Duration (iii) Day scholars for whom PEP class is starting after 01st June : The interface for booking will start from 27th May'2019 at 02:00 PM. Students can stay in the summer hostel starting from 01st Jun.'2019 and can book their seat through : UMS-> Residential and Vendor Services → Residential booking → Hostel Booking for Short Duration (b) For Admission Councellors or Interns in Division of Admissions : Student who are recruited as a Admission counseller in Div. of Admission and are hostlers will stay with the currently allocated hostel till 31st May'2019. They have to book seat again through summer hostel booking interface and also shift to their new allotted hostels on 01st Jun.'2019. Students can book the hostel-seat through : UMS-> Residential and Vendor Services → Residential booking → Hostel Booking for Short Duration (c) For Summer Term Students / Reappear/ Placement Drives/ Scrutiny/Backlog/ Viva/ Skill Development Classes/ Sports or Cultural Workshop/ Dissertation Work/ Freshmen Induction/ Training : Authorized students can book the hostel-seat through : UMS-> Residential and Vendor Services → Residential booking → Hostel Booking for Short Duration 3. Important Dates : All type of booking can be done till 10th Jul.'2019 and interface for online booking will closed on 05th Jul.'2019. 4. In this booking process, the student has to select the date of stay, check the availability of seats and then book the seats. Student can select single day or multiple days. 5. Stay is available in BH-4 ABC for Boys and GH-6 AB for Girls. Apartment facility will not be available. 6. Mode of Payment : Payment through Online Net-banking or Debit Card using online interface is available. 7. Summer Term Hostel Charges will be applicable as per the Annexure-1. 8. Other important information : (a) Student will have to pay electricity charges during booking as per the Annexure-1. Damage charges will be charged at the time of No-dues to be processed at the time of vacating the hostel. (b) Group booking facility will not be available. (c) These charges are exclusive of Food Facility. Food charges have to be paid to mess contractors directly. (d) The students can stay in hostel during Summer Vacations till 10th Jul.'19 only. On 11th Jul.'19 they will have to move to their respective allocated hostel blocks for forthcoming session 2019-20. If any day scholar has booked the hostel facility for summer duration he/ she has to vacate the hostel on 11th Jul.'19. (e) Mess/ Canteen/ Departmental store of BH-4 and GH-6 will be operational. (f) If the student did not occupy their hostel seat or cancel a seat after partial stay, no refund of the paid amount will be done. (g) Up-gradation or degradation of booked seater is not allowed hence students must select the seater preference very carefully.

Car accident is the major cause of death in which around 1.3 million people die every year. Lack of sleep or distractions like the phone call, talking with the passenger, etc may lead to an accident. To prevent such accidents this is a system which alerts the driver if the driver gets distracted or feels drowsy. 3 IoT enabled water quality monitoring system in water purifier. To make sure that safe distribution of water is done, it should be monitored in real time for new approach in IOT based water quality has been projected. Real time water quality observation is monitored by data acquisition, method and transmission with increase in the wireless device network technology in internet of things. SOLAR ENERGY S.N Name of the Project Description 1 Single axis sun tracking system A microcontroller-based project for sun tracking system for PV solar array for maximum power tracking. The tilt of the solar the panel will be changing as per the movement of the sun so as to get maximum irradiation falling on the panel. This will result in obtaining the maximum output from the installed panel. A comparative approach will be utilized so as to highlight the benefits of the sun tracking system 2 Dual axis sun tracking system This project will focus on obtaining the maximum output from the installed PV solar panel by changing the tilt angle in accordance to the variation of the solar insolation as a function of the time of the day and day of the year. So, both the horizontal axis tilt and the vertical axis tilt will be continually adjusted so to obtain the maximum power from the panels. 3 MPPT controller design The project will focus on delivering maximum power to the load connected to the PV solar system. The electrical efficiency of the PV system will be improved by developing an interface between the installed solar panel and the connected load. The objective of the interface is to track the maximum power point of the installed panel. 4 Designing of a grid-connected solar power plant in a residential complex (with and without battery storage system) The objective of the project is to estimate the capacity of the solar power plant based on the available historical load data of the given residential complex. The second key point is to decide on the physical layout of the solar farm while deciding on the size of the panel. The third key point is to decide on the battery size for the installed PV solar farm for net-zero grid power consumption 5 Designing of commercial solar power plant (grid connected) The project objective is to design a commercial solar the power plant of given capacity. The layout of the plant has to be decided as per the available estate area. The key deciding factors are the string size, no of inverters to be used, installation of AC/DC distribution boxes, grid synchronization, and protection. title: Prevention from Dengue Fever : (5/16/2019)
body: Dengue virus is transmitted by a bite from the Aedes aegypti mosquito. Only the female mosquito transmits the dengue virus. This mosquito is a daytime biter, both inside and outside homes, and is most active in the hours after sunrise and before sunset. Aedes aegypti mosquitoes breed inside and outside the home in containers holding water and rarely fly more than 200 meters from the breeding site. They do not breed in creeks, swamps, pools or other bodies of water. --Signs and symptoms This disease has a sudden onset and symptoms may include: • Fever for 3 to 7 days • Intense headache and pain behind the eyes • Muscle and joint pain • Loss of appetite • Vomiting and diarrhea • Skin rash • Bleeding, usually from the nose or gums. Recovery is sometimes associated with prolonged fatigue and depression. Repeated episodes of dengue fever may result in excessive bleeding and shock but, with appropriate treatment, are rarely fatal. --Prevention • There is no vaccine to prevent human infection by this virus. • Wear long, loose fitting, light coloured clothing, covering as much of the body as you can. Mosquitoes can bite through tight clothing like jeans. • Personal protection and the environmental management of mosquitoes are important in preventing illness. • When outdoors, apply insect repellent containing DEET (diethyl toluamide) or picaridin and always follow instructions on the label. • Place mosquito-proof mesh on doors and windows. • Cover your sleeping areas with mosquito nets. Aerosol knockdown or surface insect sprays can help control mosquitoes inside the home but always follow instructions on the label. - All hostel student/staff to ensure that Desert Cooler installed at their rooms to be kept dry when not in use.

title: Prevention from Fungal Infection : (5/14/2019)
body: Ringworm is a fungal skin infection that causes a red, circular, itchy rash. Take care of yourself to prevent this infection. title: Prevention from Dengue Fever : (5/9/2019)
body: Dengue virus is transmitted by a bite from the Aedes aegypti mosquito. Only the female mosquito transmits the dengue virus. This mosquito is a daytime biter, both inside and outside homes, and is most active in the hours after sunrise and before sunset. Aedes aegypti mosquitoes breed inside and outside the home in containers holding water and rarely fly more than 200 meters from the breeding site. They do not breed in creeks, swamps, pools or other bodies of water. --Signs and symptoms This disease has a sudden onset and symptoms may include: • Fever for 3 to 7 days • Intense headache and pain behind the eyes • Muscle and joint pain • Loss of appetite • Vomiting and diarrhea • Skin rash • Bleeding, usually from the nose or gums. Recovery is sometimes associated with prolonged fatigue and depression. Repeated episodes of dengue fever may result in excessive bleeding and shock but, with appropriate treatment, are rarely fatal. --Prevention • There is no vaccine to prevent human infection by this virus. • Wear long, loose fitting, light coloured clothing, covering as much of the body as you can. Mosquitoes can bite through tight clothing like jeans. • Personal protection and the environmental management of mosquitoes are important in preventing illness. • When outdoors, apply insect repellent containing DEET (diethyl toluamide) or picaridin and always follow instructions on the label. • Place mosquito-proof mesh on doors and windows. • Cover your sleeping areas with mosquito nets. Aerosol knockdown or surface insect sprays can help control mosquitoes inside the home but always follow instructions on the label. * All hostel student/staff to ensure that Desert Cooler installed at their rooms to be kept dry when not in use.

title: Facilities added exclusively for Hostelers from Session 2019 onwards : (5/6/2019)
body: Lovely Professional University (LPU) always strive to provide congenial and healthy environment to all the hostelers. As the new session is about to begin and students are already making choices for residential and related facilities, certain important points regarding various new options that have been made available exclusively for Hostelers are listed below: 1. Flexible Food and Mess Options: In order to provide students with more flexibility and increased choice of food varieties, the university is providing more options to the students in selecting the mess, menu etc. 2. Increase in No. of Rooms across all categories: More AC Rooms and Air cooler rooms in all categories (4/3/2/1 seater Standard and Apartment rooms) have been added so that students can get the desired choice in the current polling being done. 3. Gym Facility (Separate for Boys and Girls): Special Gym facility is being introduced at three different locations exclusively for hostelers at 50% subsidized fee. 4. Indoor Stadium: With facilities like swimming pool, warm up pool, shooting range, squash court, badminton court, volleyball court, basketball court etc. at 50% subsidized fee. 5. Open Gym: In addition to special Gym facility as mentioned above, Open Gym (without charges) is also being created. 6. Apartment Facilities (with reduced fee): Compared to last year, the fee has been reduced approximately by upto 10-15% in Apartments with the same infrastructure and facilities. In addition to fee reduction, students can take add – on facilities at nominal cost. Please refer to the attached file for details regarding above facilities. Who All Can Apply? 1. Students who have not opted for hostel till date: For Such students, the last date for polling has been extended till 10th May 2019 so that students can make choices based on various facilities that have been added exclusively for Hostelers from Session 2019. 2. Students who have already booked hostel with Rs. 1000: Students who have already opted for a particular type of room and wish to change or wants to opt for additional facilities as mentioned above, can submit the updation request through UMS. The following link for hostel booking, seater change and opting for new facilities has been active UMS Navigation >> Residential & Vendor Services >> Residential Booking >> Online Residential Booking. For any further details, Contact: Mr. Rupinder Singh, 9501110441, 01824 444361 Block 29, Room No. 301.
